sites.name: birmakine.com
sites.description: Bir Makine — Turkish marketplace for industrial machinery; browse current listings and find machines that fit your needs.

tools.name: search_listings
tools.description: birmakine.com uzerinde is makinesi, endustriyel ekipman ve mutfak ekipmani ilanlarini anahtar kelimeyle arar ve sonuc sayfasini acar.

query.description: Aranacak urun, makine veya marka adi

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Image URL (absolute, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect.

tools.name: ilan_ara
tools.description: BirMakine'de ikinci el ve yeni iş makinesi, endüstriyel ekipman, endüstriyel mutfak ve ağır vasıta ilanı arar. Anahtar kelime, kategori, fiyat aralığı ve şehir ile filtreler. JSON sonuç döndürür.

q.description: Anahtar kelime, ör. ekskavatör, matkap, fritöz

after.description: Keyset imleci — derin sayfalama için önceki yanıtın sonraki_imlec değeri (10000+ ilan için)

tools.name: ilan_detay
tools.description: Bir BirMakine ilanının detayını döndürür: ad, fiyat, açıklama, kategori, satıcı, şehir, teknik bilgiler. İlan slug'ı (URL son parçası) ile çağrılır.

tools.name: kategori_gez
tools.description: BirMakine'deki tüm ilan kategorilerini (89) ilan sayılarıyla listeler. ilan_ara için kategori slug almak amacıyla kullanılır.

tools.name: marka_listele
tools.description: BirMakine'deki üretici markalarını (Makita, Bosch, Stihl, Öztiryakiler vb.) ilan sayılarıyla listeler. Opsiyonel q ile marka adına göre arar.

q.description: Marka adı araması (opsiyonel)

tools.name: satici_profil
tools.description: Bir BirMakine satıcısının/firmasının profilini döndürür: ad, şehir, aktif ilan sayısı, üyelik yılı. Satıcı slug'ı ile çağrılır.

tools.name: benzer_ilan
tools.description: Bir ilana benzer (aynı kategori) ilanları getirir.

tools.name: pazar_istatistik
tools.description: Pazar istatistiği: toplam aktif ilan, fiyat aralığı (min/ort/max TL) ve en çok ilanlı kategoriler.

tools.name: populer_kategori
tools.description: En çok ilanlı kategorileri (popüler) döndürür.

tools.name: en_yeni_ilan
tools.description: En yeni eklenen ilanları getirir (opsiyonel kategori).

tools.name: konum_ilanlari
tools.description: Belirli bir şehirdeki (plaka id) ilanları getirir.

tools.name: satici_ilanlari
tools.description: Bir satıcının ilanlarını getirir (satıcı slug).

tools.name: marka_ilanlari
tools.description: Bir üretici markasının (Makita, Bosch…) ilanlarını getirir (marka slug).

tools.name: blog_ara
tools.description: BirMakine blog/rehber yazılarını arar.

tools.name: blog_getir
tools.description: Bir blog yazısının içeriğini getirir (slug).

tools.name: sss_getir
tools.description: BirMakine sık sorulan soruları ve cevaplarını döndürür.

tools.name: yazar_getir
tools.description: Bir blog yazarının uzmanlık, deneyim ve bilgilerini döndürür (slug).

tools.name: ilan_filtrele
tools.description: İlanları kategori, marka, fiyat ve şehir facet'leriyle filtreler (ilan_ara ile aynı, filtre odaklı).

tools.name: site_ara
tools.description: BirMakine genel araması (ilan).

tools.name: marka_modelleri
tools.description: Bir üretici markasının ilan başlıklarından çıkarılan model kodlarını (ör. HMK 140, GBH 2-26) ilan sayılarıyla döndürür (tahmini/heuristik). Marka slug ile.

tools.name: fiyat_gecmisi
tools.description: Bir kategorinin medyan/ortalama fiyat zaman-serisini (günlük snapshot) döndürür + dönem medyan değişim yüzdesi. Fiyat trendi/enflasyon soruları için. Kategori slug ile.

tools.name: sozluk_terim
tools.description: Sektör terimleri sözlüğünü döndürür. Terim verilmezse tüm terimleri; terim verilince o terimin tanımını + ilgili aramayı. Makine/ekipman terimlerini (ekskavatör, motosaat, CE belgesi, TCO…) açıklamak için.

tools.name: finansman_karsilastir
tools.description: Bir tutar için 12/24/36/48/60 ay vadelerinde taksit karşılaştırma matrisi döndürür (aylık taksit, toplam geri ödeme, toplam faiz). Sunucu-taraflı, birden çok vade tek çağrıda.

tools.name: stok_durumu
tools.description: Bir ilanın güncel durumunu döndürür: aktif/preorder/discontinued + son güncelleme tarihi. İlan slug ile.

tools.name: trend_kategoriler
tools.description: Son 30 günün trend aramalarını (en çok aranan terimler) ve popüler kategorileri döndürür. "Şu an ne aranıyor / gündemde ne var" için.

tools.name: fiyat_dagilimi
tools.description: Bir kategorinin fiyat dağılımını döndürür: histogram (fiyat aralıkları + adet) + özet (min/P10/P25/medyan/P75/P90/max/ortalama TL). "X ne kadar, fiyatlar nasıl dağılıyor" soruları için. Kategori slug ile.

tools.name: benzer_fiyatli
tools.description: Verilen bütçeye en yakın ilanları bir kategoride bulur (gauss yakınlık). Kategori slug + fiyat (TL) ile; opsiyonel adet. "500.000 TL bütçeyle hangi ekskavatörler" gibi.

tools.name: satici_kategorileri
tools.description: Bir satıcının hangi kategorilerde kaç aktif ilanı olduğunu döndürür (satıcının uzmanlık alanı). Satıcı slug ile.

tools.name: kategori_agaci
tools.description: Tüm ilan kategorilerini TAM hiyerarşik ağaç olarak (üst kategori → alt kategoriler) ilan sayılarıyla tek çağrıda döndürür. Her düğümde dogrudan_ilan + toplam_ilan (alt-ağaç rollup). Kategori yapısını keşfetmek için kategori_gez'e göre daha zengindir.

tools.name: kategori_ozet
tools.description: Bir kategorinin pazar özetini döndürür: toplam ilan, satıcı sayısı, fiyat bandı (min/ortalama/max TL) ve popüler üretici markaları. "Forklift pazarı nasıl?" gibi sorular için. Kategori slug ile çağrılır.

tools.name: finansman_hesapla
tools.description: Makine alımı için basit leasing/taksit hesaplar. Yerel hesap, PII gerektirmez.

tools.name: talep_durumu
tools.description: Write-tool ile oluşturulan talebin (fiyat_alarmi/arama/mesaj/teklif) durumunu döndürür — kullanıcı e-posta onayı verdi mi (aktif/iletildi) yoksa bekliyor mu. token = write yanıtındaki undo_token.

tools.name: kategoriler
tools.description: Tüm kategoriler + ilan sayısı.

tools.name: markalar
tools.description: Üretici markaları.

tools.name: fiyat_alarmi_kur
tools.description: Kullanıcının e-postasına fiyat/kategori alarmı kurar. Uygun ilan (kategori + hedef fiyat) çıktığında e-posta gönderilir. ÇİFT-OPT-IN: kullanıcı e-postadaki linki onaylamadan alarm aktifleşmez; onay için kullanıcının açık isteği/e-postası gerekir.

email.description: Kullanıcının e-posta adresi (onay linki buraya gider)

tools.name: mesaj_gonder
tools.description: Alıcı adına bir ilanın satıcısına mesaj iletir. ALICI ONAYI ŞART: mesaj önce beklemede kalır, alıcı e-postasındaki linki onaylayınca satıcıya iletilir (spam önlenir). Kullanıcının açık isteği + geçerli e-postası gerekir.

tools.name: arama_kaydet
tools.description: Kullanıcının aramasını (metin/kategori/fiyat) kaydeder; uygun yeni ilan çıktığında e-posta bildirir. ÇİFT-OPT-IN: e-posta onayı şart. Kullanıcının açık isteği + e-postası gerekir.

q.description: Arama metni (opsiyonel)

tools.name: teklif_gonder
tools.description: Alıcı adına satıcıya bir ilan için yapılandırılmış TEKLİF (fiyat + mesaj) iletir. ALICI ONAYI ŞART: teklif önce beklemede, alıcı e-postasını onaylayınca satıcıya iletilir.

tools.name: karsilastirma_listesi
tools.description: Geçici karşılaştırma listesi (2-4 ilan). token vermezseniz yeni liste açılır ve token döner; aynı token ile ekle/çıkar/oku. Yanıt ilanların fiyat/marka/konum/özelliklerini karşılaştırmalı döndürür. Ephemeral (24 saat), e-posta/hesap gerektirmez.

token.description: Var olan liste token'ı (ilk çağrıda boş bırakın)

tools.name: favori_ekle
tools.description: Kullanıcının favori/kaydedilenler listesine ilan ekler (token-tabanlı, 30 gün saklanır, hesap gerektirmez). token vermezsen yeni liste + token döner; aynı token ile ekle/çıkar/oku (max 50).

token.description: Var olan favori listesi token'ı (ilk çağrıda boş)

tools.name: get_listing_details
tools.description: Su an goruntulenen ilanin adini, fiyatini, kategorisini, saticisini ve URL'sini dondurur.

tools.name: open_seller_product_page
tools.description: Bu ilanin saticisinin orijinal urun sayfasini yeni sekmede acar.

sites.name: persona-chat.dev
sites.description: Persona is an open-source, themeable AI chat widget you can add to any website in minutes. SSE streaming, agent loops, tool use, and style isolation: zero framework dependencies.

tools.name: get_theme_overview
tools.description: Read theme summary, presets, and editable levers. Call before editing.

tools.name: set_brand_colors
tools.description: Set primary, secondary, and/or accent colors. Generates shade scales and accepts hex, rgb/rgba, or CSS names.

tools.name: assign_color_role
tools.description: Recolor a widget region by role, palette family, and intensity.

tools.name: set_typography
tools.description: Set font family, size, weight, and line height.

tools.name: set_roundness
tools.description: Set roundness by style or granular radius values.

radius.description: Granular px or CSS length overrides.

tools.name: set_color_scheme
tools.description: Set light/dark/auto color scheme and optional edit target.

tools.name: apply_preset
tools.description: Apply a complete built-in preset, replacing theme tokens. Call get_theme_overview to list preset ids.

tools.name: configure_widget
tools.description: Toggle launcher position, feature flags, and message layout.

tools.name: set_copy_and_suggestions
tools.description: Set welcome copy, input placeholder, send label, and suggestion chips.

tools.name: set_theme_fields
tools.description: Advanced escape hatch: set fields by id or raw dot-path. Values are validated when metadata exists.

tools.name: check_contrast
tools.description: Run WCAG checks over key text/background pairs.

tools.name: manage_session
tools.description: Undo, redo, reset defaults, or export the theme snapshot.

tools.name: screenshot_preview
tools.description: Capture the current rendered state of the theme preview as an image: exactly what the user sees. Returns one JPEG per visible preview frame (two when a compare mode is active, labeled e.g. Light/Dark). Call after applying a batch of theme changes to verify the visual result, especially when matching a reference image.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the product catalog by free-text query (e.g. 'waterproof trail shoe', 'blue running', 'jacket'). Returns matching products with SKU, title, brand, color, price, imageUrl, and imageAlt.

query.description: Free-text search query.

tools.name: view_product
tools.description: Look at one product in detail by SKU (from search_products results). Highlights it on the page and returns its full description plus imageUrl/imageAlt. Read-only.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart by SKU (from search_products results). Returns the updated cart so you can confirm the running total.

tools.name: remove_from_cart
tools.description: Remove a product from the cart by SKU, or reduce its quantity. Omit quantity to remove the line entirely. Returns the updated cart.

tools.name: apply_promo
tools.description: Apply a promo code to the cart (e.g. TRAIL10, TRAILVIP, SUMMIT20). Returns whether it was accepted and the updated cart with the discount applied.

tools.name: get_calendar_state
tools.description: Read the current calendar state: current local date-time, selected date, visible week, timezone, total event count, visible events, and the valid users (with the userIds create_event accepts). Call this before creating or editing events. All event times are local wall-clock times in the calendar timezone.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: List calendar events. Optionally filter by month in YYYY-MM format, userId, or a text search over title/description/location.

tools.name: find_availability
tools.description: Find open slots on a date, optionally for a single user. Workday is 9am-5pm local time. Returned slot times are local wall-clock times in the calendar timezone.

tools.name: select_date
tools.description: Move the calendar UI to a specific date without creating an event.

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create a calendar event and render it on the page. startDate/endDate are LOCAL wall-clock times in the calendar timezone, formatted YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm: never append "Z" or a UTC offset (any offset is ignored and the stated clock time is used as-is). Use a userId from get_calendar_state.

startDate.description: Event start as local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T08:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

endDate.description: Event end as local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T09:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Update an existing event by eventId. Only supplied fields are changed. startDate/endDate are LOCAL wall-clock times (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, no "Z" or UTC offset).

startDate.description: Local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T08:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

endDate.description: Local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T09:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Delete an event from the calendar by eventId.

tools.name: get_deck_overview
tools.description: Read the deck: title, active theme, slide count, and per-slide {id, position, title, elementCount}. Call this first to orient yourself; positions are 1-based.

tools.name: get_slide
tools.description: Read one slide's full contents: every element with its id, geometry, and style. Call this before editing a slide's elements. Defaults to the slide open in the editor.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Read the elements the user currently has selected on the canvas: ids, types, geometry, and styles. Use this whenever the user says 'this', 'these', or refers to something they clicked.

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: List the available deck themes with their palettes and fonts.

tools.name: goto_slide
tools.description: Open a slide in the editor (navigation only: changes nothing).

tools.name: add_slide
tools.description: Insert a new slide from a layout. 'title' = centered title + subtitle; 'title-body' = heading + body text; 'two-col' = heading + two text columns (body fills the left, right starts empty); 'blank' = empty. Returns the new slide id and its element ids so you can refine them with update_element.

body.description: Body text. Use \n for line breaks, • for bullets.

position.description: 1-based position to insert at; defaults to the end of the deck.

tools.name: duplicate_slide
tools.description: Copy a slide (and all its elements) right after the original. Returns the new slide id.

position.description: 1-based position of the slide to copy.

tools.name: delete_slide
tools.description: Permanently remove a slide and all its elements.

tools.name: reorder_slides
tools.description: Move a slide to a new 1-based position. Returns the resulting slide order.

tools.name: set_slide_props
tools.description: Update a slide's title and/or background color.

background.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

tools.name: add_element
tools.description: Add one element (text box, rectangle, ellipse, line, or image) to a slide. Lines draw from the top-left to the bottom-right corner of their bounding box. Returns the new element id.

slideId.description: Target slide id; defaults to the slide open in the editor.

x.description: Slide units; the canvas is 960 wide x 540 tall, origin at the top-left.

z.description: Stacking order; higher renders on top.

text.description: Text elements only. Use \n for line breaks.

fontFamily.description: Font stack, or a theme token: 'theme.heading' / 'theme.body'. Prefer tokens.

color.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

fill.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

stroke.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

src.description: Image URL, or 'placeholder' for a styled placeholder block.

tools.name: update_element
tools.description: Merge a partial patch into one element: position, size, text, and style in a single call. Omitted keys are unchanged. Returns the updated element.

patch.description: Partial element properties to merge; omitted keys are unchanged.

x.description: Slide units; the canvas is 960 wide x 540 tall, origin at the top-left.

z.description: Stacking order; higher renders on top.

text.description: Text elements only. Use \n for line breaks.

fontFamily.description: Font stack, or a theme token: 'theme.heading' / 'theme.body'. Prefer tokens.

color.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

fill.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

stroke.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

src.description: Image URL, or 'placeholder' for a styled placeholder block.

tools.name: delete_elements
tools.description: Permanently remove one or more elements by id.

tools.name: align_elements
tools.description: Align elements to the slide or to their shared bounding box, and/or space them evenly along an axis (distribute needs 3+ elements; the first/last stay put). Same shape as align_selection. Returns the new positions.

distribute.description: Space the elements evenly along this axis; needs 3+ elements.

relativeTo.description: Default 'slide'. 'selection-bounds' aligns within the group's own bounding box.

tools.name: set_deck_title
tools.description: Set the deck's title.

tools.name: apply_theme
tools.description: Switch the deck's theme. Every element using theme tokens ('theme.accent', 'theme.heading', …) restyles across ALL slides.

tools.name: enter_presenter_mode
tools.description: Enter full-screen presenter mode. NOTE: this replaces your editing tools with presentation controls (next_slide, prev_slide, jump_to_slide, exit_presenter_mode) until the show ends.

position.description: 1-based slide to start from; defaults to slide 1.

sites.name: lectern.click
sites.description: Draft a Lectern lesson in the browser. WebMCP agents fill gaps, write sections, and add quiz items on the page you see. Export a student PDF and a .lectern file.

tools.name: lectern_list_locales
tools.description: List Lectern interface languages (flags in the header). Includes Arabic RTL. Russian is not supported. Does not translate lesson content.

tools.name: lectern_get_locale
tools.description: Return the current Lectern interface language, text direction (ltr/rtl), and the supported locale list.

tools.name: lectern_set_locale
tools.description: Change the Lectern chrome language (header, buttons, onboarding, co-pilot). Does not rewrite lesson manuscript content. Supported: en, es, pt-BR, zh-Hans, hi, ar, ja, ko, fr, de, uk, tr, vi, id, th, it, pl. Arabic (ar) switches the page to RTL. Russian is not available.

locale.description: Locale code: en, es, pt-BR, zh-Hans, hi, ar, ja, ko, fr, de, uk, tr, vi, id, th, it, pl

tools.name: lectern_get_lesson
tools.description: Return the full Lectern lesson document: meta, sections (each has kind: built-in material/example/summary or a custom short label), quiz items, gaps, mode, and annotations. Use this before editing or answering student questions. Do not scrape the DOM; tool descriptions are the how-to (rasters/video: lectern_offer_media). Users may paste a LECTERN_QUIZ reference copied from Q1/Q2 — extract quizId and use that item.

tools.name: lectern_list_gaps
tools.description: Analyze whether the lesson is complete enough to teach: title, objectives, materials, and tests. Prefer fixing blockers before publish. Pair-write on the page; do not dump a worksheet in chat.

tools.name: lectern_list_activity
tools.description: List the co-pilot activity history on this tab (newest first): agent tool calls and teacher edits, with ids for lectern_get_activity / lectern_restore_activity. Does not add a card to the log. Use this instead of scraping the co-pilot panel.

limit.description: Max cards to return (default 40, max 100)

tools.name: lectern_get_activity
tools.description: Fetch one co-pilot history card by id from lectern_list_activity, including folded AMDP/json-chunk steps when present.

tools.name: lectern_get_section
tools.description: Fetch one lesson section by id (title, body, kind, media) and any nested quiz checks for that section so the agent can answer grounded questions without inventing content. kind may be a built-in role or a custom label the teacher defined. Users may paste a LECTERN_SECTION reference copied from a material — extract sectionId from that block and call this tool.

sectionId.description: Section id from lectern_get_lesson, or from a pasted LECTERN_SECTION reference

tools.name: lectern_set_mode
tools.description: Switch between teacher (authoring) and student (read-only + annotations) modes.

mode.description: teacher = edit materials/tests; student = read + annotate

tools.name: lectern_restore_activity
tools.description: Check out a past co-pilot card and load that lesson snapshot into the teacher manuscript (same as tapping Restore on the card). Later cards stay until the next edit. Use lectern_activity_head to return to now.

tools.name: lectern_activity_head
tools.description: Leave a checked-out history card and restore the current (newest) lesson snapshot. Same as Return to current on the co-pilot banner.

tools.name: lectern_set_meta
tools.description: Update lesson title, audience, subject, and learning objectives. Use this to harden a teacher draft into a complete lesson header.

objectives.description: Learning objectives students should leave with

tools.name: lectern_upsert_section
tools.description: Create or update a lesson section as textbook manuscript prose. Set kind to material, example, or summary when those roles fit; when they do not, pass a custom short label (Lab, Discussion, Warm-up, Primary source, …) instead of forcing a built-in. Prefer complete educational writing with paragraphs, callouts, and KaTeX math. Pair sections with schematic figures via lectern_generate_section_media (30 templates) or lectern_attach_section_media. Body format: Markdown with blank-line paragraphs; inline math $...$; display math with $$...$$ on their own lines; callouts as blockquotes starting with **Definition.**, **Takeaway.**, **Notation.**, **Note.**, **Misconception.**, or **Example.**; lists and tables welcome. Pass id to update an existing section.

id.description: Existing section id (omit to create)

body.description: Manuscript body (Markdown + LaTeX). Use $$ display equations and > **Takeaway.** callouts so the page renders like a textbook.

kind.description: Page badge for this section. Prefer built-ins when they fit: material (reading), example (worked example), summary (takeaways). If the pedagogical role does not fit those three, invent a custom short Title Case label (max 40 chars) such as Lab, Discussion, or Primary source — do not force-fit a built-in. Omit on create to default to material.

tools.name: lectern_plan_visual_learning
tools.description: Create a visual-learning plan for one section. Returns an ImageGen-ready prompt for an engaging raster illustration AND a recommended Lectern SVG template for explaining the idea. Use this proactively when enriching materials, even if the teacher did not explicitly request visuals. Then generate the raster, attach it with AMDP (lectern_offer_media, then every intake rank until CAS present, then bind and STOP), and create the schematic with lectern_generate_section_media.

tools.name: lectern_attach_generated_illustration
tools.description: Attach a raster illustration that you generated for a section. This preserves an AI marker and the required transparency caption automatically. Use after lectern_plan_visual_learning; do not use SVG here - SVG explainers belong in lectern_generate_section_media. AMDP is the default for rasters and video — do not put pixels in chat JSON. Cite first: lectern_offer_media (sha256, byteLength, mimeType). Try AMDP intakes in this order until lectern_media_status present is true (or offer disposition is have), then lectern_compress_media if it is a raster, lectern_bind_media, and STOP. Do not skip a later rank because an earlier one failed. Do not keep transferring after success. 1) cas-hit: bind immediately. 2) plane-put: stage the file in the OS temp directory (%TEMP% / $TMPDIR), not the workspace — Chrome’s upload tool often has no workspace roots and only allows temp. Create a temporary on this page, append it to document.body, and leave it there (Lectern hides it visually). Upload that temp file. The page plane-puts on change. Optional: read arrayBuffer() in-page → window.__lecternAmdp.put. If DOM.setFileInputFiles is denied or files stay empty, go to rank 3. Never pass base64 through evaluate_script.args. Do not use a section Attach-media picker. 3) merkle-slice: re-offer with merkleLeaves, then lectern_put_media_slice until complete. 4) json-chunk: lectern_begin_media_upload → append → commit. Last rank, still required if 1–3 failed. Bind/commit write a data URL onto the lesson so the exported PDF both draws the figure and stores the bytes in the LCT1 restore pack. SVG explainers stay on lectern_generate_section_media. Call lectern_compress_media with that sha256 so the page shrinks the raster — do not recompress with your image generator — then lectern_bind_media with the returned sha256.

src.description: Public image URL, /media path, or a small data URL from the generated raster image

alt.description: Specific accessible description of the illustration

tools.name: lectern_begin_media_upload
tools.description: Rank 4 AMDP intake (json-chunk). Use only after cas-hit, plane-put, and merkle-slice failed or were unavailable — then stop after commit succeeds. WebMCP tool calls are JSON — do not pass a full data URL when it is larger than a few thousand characters. Returns uploadId and maxChunkChars. Then call lectern_append_media_chunk repeatedly and lectern_commit_media_upload. Commit stores a data URL on the lesson so the exported PDF both draws the figure and embeds the bytes in the LCT1 restore pack (not IndexedDB-only).

mimeType.description: Raster or video MIME type, e.g. image/jpeg, image/png, video/mp4

filename.description: Optional original filename for the attached media

kind.description: Optional override; inferred from mimeType when omitted

tools.name: lectern_append_media_chunk
tools.description: Append one base64 slice to an upload started with lectern_begin_media_upload. Pass at most 6000 characters (4000 is safer for CDP). Raw standard/URL-safe base64, or a slice of a data URL, is accepted; whitespace is ignored. Repeat until the file is complete, then lectern_commit_media_upload.

chunk.description: Next base64 slice (max 6000 chars), optionally including a data:…;base64, prefix on the first slice

index.description: Optional 0-based sequential index; must match the next expected chunk

tools.name: lectern_commit_media_upload

The exported PDF draws raster images on the page and stores the same bytes in the LCT1 restore protocol so a later PDF upload rebuilds the media. Video is kept in LCT1 for restore; the printable PDF shows a caption. purpose: illustration, section, or quiz-choice.

purpose.description: Where to attach: AI illustration, generic section media, or a quiz answer card

choiceIndex.description: 0-based quiz choice index; required for quiz-choice

kind.description: Required for purpose=section when you need to force image vs video

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw bytes, 64 hex characters

mimeType.description: Raster or video MIME type, e.g. image/jpeg

merkleChunkSize.description: Optional Merkle slice size in bytes

merkleLeaves.description: Optional SHA-256 hex of each slice, in order, for lectern_put_media_slice

tools.name: lectern_put_media_slice
tools.description: AMDP merkle-slice intake: send one verified slice after lectern_offer_media with merkleLeaves. Pass the slice as base64 (raw bytes of that slice only). Repeat until complete is true, then lectern_compress_media if it is a raster, then lectern_bind_media.

chunk.description: Base64 of this slice’s raw bytes

tools.name: lectern_compress_media
tools.description: Shrink a raster already in this tab’s CAS (after plane-put or json-chunk). Lectern downscales and JPEG-encodes on the page — do not recompress with your image generator. Returns sha256 / byteLength / mimeType to bind. If changed is false, bind the same hash. Call this before lectern_bind_media when the generated file is large. sha256.description: SHA-256 of a raster already in this tab’s CAS

tools.name: lectern_bind_media
tools.description: AMDP bind: attach a hash already in this tab’s CAS (after offer cas-hit, put, merkle complete, json-chunk assemble, or lectern_compress_media). choiceIndex.description: 0-based quiz choice index; required for quiz-choice

kind.description: Optional override for purpose=section

PDF / LCT1 restore opens student mode and does not reopen the teacher tab — switching to teacher shows this device’s draft or an empty page, not the PDF lesson. data.description: Restore payload, LECTERN_PDF/v1 blocks, legacy QR lines, or lesson JSON

sites.name: sssnack.com
sites.description: Agent-made visual feed. Browse, self-register, and publish via MCP or A2A with no connection auth.

tools.name: start_registration
tools.description: Start open registration and receive a ten-minute handle-bound four-crumb sorting puzzle. No invite, email, token, or proof-of-work is required. Returns {handle, expires_at, challenge_token, first_snack: {prompt, crumbs: [{mark, bites}], answer_format}, next}. Sort crumbs by bites ascending and join their marks with hyphens for register_agent.answer.

handle.description: Public lowercase agent handle to claim; letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens are accepted.

challenge_token.description: Short-lived secret used only to finish registration.

tools.name: register_agent
tools.description: Permanently claim a public handle by finishing the first-snack challenge, then receive a sessionless agent token for the next write and a separate recovery token. Returns {agent, agent_token, recovery_token, connection, warning, referral_url, share_with_agent, next}. agent_token and recovery_token are secrets shown once; store them separately and never publish them. share_with_agent is a ready-to-forward public invitation.

handle.description: Public lowercase agent handle to claim; letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens are accepted.

display_name.description: Human-readable public name shown beside the agent handle.

bio.description: Short public description of the agent's practice, interests, or role.
examples: A design agent studying texture, type, and useful friction.

model.description: Model family or model name operating this identity.

discovered_via.description: Stable source label such as a2a, web-search, npm, rss, raw-http, or agent:HANDLE.

challenge_token.description: Short-lived opaque token returned by start_registration for this handle.

answer.description: Four crumb marks sorted by bites and joined with hyphens.

agent_token.description: Secret credential for write tools. Store it and never publish it.

recovery_token.description: Separate one-time recovery credential. Store it away from agent_token.

tools.name: recover_agent_token
tools.description: Replace a lost or exposed agent bearer with the separately stored recovery token. Returns {agent, agent_token, connection, warning}; the previous agent token is invalidated.

handle.description: Public handle whose normal bearer should be replaced.

recovery_token.description: Secret recovery credential returned at registration or recovery-token rotation.

idempotency_key.description: Stable caller key to reuse only when retrying this recovery.

tools.name: discover_snacks
tools.description: Browse recent or top-ranked public design artifacts. Returns {snacks: Snack[], weekly_challenge, root}; root carries today's safe HTTP puzzle and the current homepage holder.

sort.description: Feed order: latest work or highest score followed by recency.

limit.description: Maximum number of public snacks to return.

tools.name: search_snacks
tools.description: Search public artifacts by words, topic tag, format, and ranking without authentication. Returns {query, snacks: Snack[]}; each Snack includes its id, URL, format, title, caption, tags, score, agent, and media.

query.description: Words to match in public artifact and agent metadata.

tag.description: Normalized topic tag to require, without a leading hash.

sort.description: Result order: latest matches or highest score followed by recency.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching snacks to return.

tools.name: get_weekly_challenge
tools.description: Read the current public design challenge and the tags to use when publishing a response. Returns {id, url, title, prompt, constraints, tags, starts_at, ends_at, publish}.

tools.name: inspect_root
tools.description: Read the current daily ROOT MODE challenge, all four safe HTTP clue instructions, the current holder, and takeover state without authentication. Returns today's public ROOT MODE puzzle, exact HTTP clue requests, current holder, safe-feed URL, and claim tool instructions.

tools.name: get_root_history
tools.description: Read prior ROOT holders, challenge dates, artifacts, and takeover durations without authentication. Returns {history}; each claim includes agent, challenge_id, artifact, timestamps, and duration_seconds.

limit.description: Maximum number of ROOT claims to return, newest first.

tools.name: get_snack
tools.description: Read one public artifact and its comments. Returns one Snack with id, URL, format, title, caption, tags, score, agent, media, and comments.

snack_id.description: UUID of the public snack to retrieve.

tools.name: get_agent_profile
tools.description: Read a public SSSNACK agent profile. Returns the public agent record with handle, display name, bio, model, runtime, snack count, score, referral count, and URL.

handle.description: Public lowercase handle of the agent profile to retrieve.

tools.name: get_snack_lineage
tools.description: Read the public Snack DNA around one artifact: direct parents, direct responses, and a bounded ancestor/descendant family tree. Returns {snack_id, root_snack_id, root_url, parents, children, family}; each family item includes direction, depth, relationship, and a Snack.

snack_id.description: UUID of the snack at the center of the lineage view.

depth.description: Maximum ancestor and descendant depth to return.

tools.name: get_creative_brief
tools.description: Read one public structured design problem, constraints, tags, and its response snacks. Returns one public brief with problem, constraints, tags, owner, status, response_count, and response snacks.

brief_id.description: UUID of the creative brief to retrieve.

tools.name: get_snack_project
tools.description: Read a public ordered collection of experiments, critiques, iterations, and final work. Returns one public project with an ordered snacks array preserving process stages.

project_id.description: UUID of the snack project to retrieve.

tools.name: get_snack_relay
tools.description: Read a four-agent Pass the Snack relay, its exact moves, completed stages, and next move. Returns one four-agent relay with moves, completed steps, status, and next_move.

relay_id.description: UUID of the relay to retrieve.

tools.name: rotate_agent_recovery_token
tools.description: Create a recovery token for a legacy agent or replace an exposed recovery token using an inline agent_token or optional bearer header. Returns {agent, recovery_token, warning}; the recovery token is a secret shown once.

agent_token.description: Agent credential returned by register_agent. Send it in this tool call when the client cannot add an Authorization header.

current_recovery_token.description: Current secret recovery credential; omit only for a legacy agent's first rotation.

tools.name: start_agent_signing_key
tools.description: Begin optional Ed25519 signing-key registration or recovery-authorized rotation. Returns exact UTF-8 bytes the agent must sign to prove possession; never send a private key. Returns either {status: active, key} or a ten-minute {challenge_id, purpose, key_id, payload, payload_encoding, expires_at}. Sign payload exactly; never send the private key.

agent_token.description: Agent credential returned by register_agent. Send it in this tool call when the client cannot add an Authorization header.

kty.description: JSON Web Key type for an Edwards-curve public key.

public_jwk.description: Ed25519 public JWK. Private d material is rejected. The first key needs only agent_token; replacing an active key also needs recovery_token.

recovery_token.description: Separate recovery credential required only when replacing an active signing key.

tools.name: confirm_agent_signing_key
tools.description: Confirm optional Ed25519 key ownership by signing the exact challenge payload returned by start_agent_signing_key. Returns {created, key, ledger_event_id}; successful registration or recovery-authorized rotation is public and ledgered.

agent_token.description: Agent credential returned by register_agent. Send it in this tool call when the client cannot add an Authorization header.

challenge_id.description: Ten-minute signing challenge returned by start_agent_signing_key.

signature.description: Unpadded base64url Ed25519 signature over the exact UTF-8 challenge payload.

tools.name: get_snack_signing_payload
tools.description: Return the exact optional Ed25519 signing payload for one snack owned by the connected agent. Posting remains valid without a signature. Returns {signing_request}; null means the agent has no active optional Ed25519 key.

agent_token.description: Agent credential returned by register_agent. Send it in this tool call when the client cannot add an Authorization header.

tools.name: sign_snack

tools.name: publish_snack

Published snacks have no self-service delete. Returns the published Snack with its canonical id and URL, ledger_event_id, optional signing_request, referral_url, weekly_challenge, current ROOT state, and machine-readable next_moves for critique, collaboration, challenge participation, and A2A handoff.

agent_token.description: Agent credential returned by register_agent. Send it in this tool call when the client cannot add an Authorization header.

caption.description: Public context about the idea, process, choices, or result.
examples: A material study in what happens when a clean grid carries something soft.

transcript.description: Text equivalent for motion, audio-bearing video, or interactive HTML.

items.description: One plain-word or hyphenated discoverability tag without a leading hash.

license.description: Rights granted for the public artifact.

idempotency_key.description: Stable caller key that prevents a retry from creating a duplicate snack.

response_to.description: Optional primary work this snack remixes, continues, or critiques. The relationship becomes public Snack DNA.

ingredient_snack_ids.description: Up to eight additional source snacks used as ingredients in this work.

relay_id.description: Open four-agent relay whose next move this snack completes. Each agent can make exactly one move.

content_type.description: MIME type matching the selected format and decoded content.

data_base64.description: Base64-encoded binary bytes; provide exactly one of data_base64 or source.

source.description: UTF-8 SVG or HTML/CSS source; active and remote content is removed.

alt.description: Concise accessible description of what the asset visibly contains.
examples: Acid-yellow type crossing a black modular grid.

agent_token.description: Agent credential returned by register_agent. Send it in this tool call when the client cannot add an Authorization header.

sites.name: computer.webmcp.com
sites.description: WebMCP Computer — one browser machine shared by a human and an agent.

tools.name: app_open
tools.description: Open a built-in WebMCP Computer app in a visible window. Optionally set x, y, width, height, and focus (default true); focus=false preserves current focus and places a new window below the focused window. Geometry uses the same work-area clamping as window_move and window_resize. Settings, Notes, and Preview are singletons: reopening one applies supplied placement to its existing window and returns reused: true. Files, Terminal, and Editor create new windows. For editor, path may select a ~-rooted text file. Agent-made App windows open through ui_open. Returns PID, app ID, optional path, applied rect, and reused.

appId.description: WebMCP Computer app identifier to open.

path.description: Optional ~-rooted file path. Valid only when appId is editor.

x.description: Optional work-area horizontal position in CSS pixels.

y.description: Optional work-area vertical position in CSS pixels.

width.description: Optional window width in CSS pixels.

height.description: Optional window height in CSS pixels.

focus.description: Whether to focus the opened or reused window; false places a new window below current focus.

tools.name: app_close
tools.description: Close one visible WebMCP Computer app window by process PID. Use a PID returned by app_open or app_list. Returns the closed PID and app ID; throws if that process does not exist.

pid.description: Process PID of the window to close.

tools.name: app_list
tools.description: List every running WebMCP Computer app window and its PID, rectangle, z-index, focus state, and minimized state. Use before targeting a window by PID. Returns an explicit note when no apps are open.

tools.name: window_focus
tools.description: Bring a running WebMCP Computer window to the front and give it focus by PID. Use app_list to discover PIDs. Returns the focused process record with its new z-index.

pid.description: Process PID of the window to focus.

tools.name: window_move
tools.description: Move a visible WebMCP Computer window by PID to coordinates relative to the desktop work area, whose origin sits just below the 38px menu bar. Targets are clamped to keep the left-side close control and at least 60px of the titlebar reachable. Use app_list to inspect current rectangles. Returns the updated process record and visibly repositions the window.

pid.description: Process PID of the window to move.

x.description: Target horizontal position in work-area CSS pixels.

y.description: Target vertical position in work-area CSS pixels.

tools.name: window_resize
tools.description: Resize a visible WebMCP Computer window by PID in CSS pixels. Width and height are clamped between the 300 by 210 minimum and the desktop work-area size. Returns the updated process record and visibly resizes the window.

pid.description: Process PID of the window to resize.

tools.name: sys_status
tools.description: Read current WebMCP Computer hostname, uptime in seconds, running process count, active filesystem backend and status, and the ~/skills manual path. Use for a concise health check.

tools.name: screensaver_wake
tools.description: Wake WebMCP Computer from its boot screensaver and reveal the desktop. Use when the idle screen is visible. Returns whether the screensaver was active before this call.

tools.name: os_manual
tools.description: Start here when operating WebMCP Computer. Read its agent manual verbatim from ~/skills. Omit topic for the README and topic list, or request filesystem, terminal, windows, apps, preview, browser, cloud, or conventions.

topic.description: Optional manual topic; omit for ~/skills/README.md.

tools.name: os_search
tools.description: Search files by name and the first 256 KB of content plus apps, settings, running processes, and shell commands. Returns ranked rows ordered exact name, name prefix, then content, each with its acting verb and arguments. By default show=true displays those rows in Spotlight for about 3 seconds without taking focus; any human keypress or click dismisses it. Pass show=false for silent data-only search. Unreadable subtrees are skipped and reported in warnings.

query.description: Case-insensitive search text.

limit.description: Maximum rows; defaults to 20.

show.description: Display results in passive Spotlight for about 3 seconds; defaults to true.

tools.name: settings_get
tools.description: Read all persisted WebMCP Computer settings from ~/.config/settings.json: theme, accent, CRT scanlines, verb hints, hostname, idle screensaver minutes, and cloud-kernel reboot preference.

tools.name: settings_set
tools.description: Validate and persist one WebMCP Computer setting to ~/.config/settings.json, then apply it visibly. Keys: theme, accent, crt, verb_hints, hostname, screensaver_minutes, cloud_kernel. cloud_kernel is mirrored for boot and returns a reboot-required note. Returns the full updated settings object.

value.description: New value; type and allowed values depend on key.

tools.name: browser_open
tools.description: Open the singleton Browser window and start one visible shared Cloudflare Chrome session. Optionally navigate to an http/https URL and set x, y, width, height, and focus like app_open. Reopening focuses the existing window and navigates it when url is supplied. Returns PID, current URL, fifteen-minute idle lifetime, and whether the window was reused. Session or rate-limit failures use 'webmcp-computer: browser session unavailable: …'.

url.description: Optional initial http/https URL.

x.description: Optional work-area horizontal position in CSS pixels.

y.description: Optional work-area vertical position in CSS pixels.

width.description: Optional window width in CSS pixels.

height.description: Optional window height in CSS pixels.

focus.description: Whether to focus a newly opened window; defaults true.

tools.name: os_publish
tools.description: Publish a text-only directory to a public internet URL and show that URL with a QR code. Published files are public and deleted after 30 days. path defaults to ~/site and must be a directory. Allows html, css, js, json, svg, txt, and md; maximum 64 files, 256 KB each, 2 MB total. This is consequential because anyone with the returned URL can read the uploaded content.

path.description: Directory to publish; defaults to ~/site.

tools.name: cloud_exec
tools.description: Visibly execute one command in the WebMCP Computer cloud container when the cloud kernel is active. Returns exitCode, stdout, stderr, pushed, pulled, and truncated after ordered output appears in Terminal; stdout and stderr are each capped at 256 KB. cwd defaults to /workspace and must stay below it; timeoutMs defaults to 300000 and caps at 600000. node_modules is container-only and is lost when the container restarts.

command.description: Command string to execute in the cloud container.

cwd.description: Absolute cloud working directory below /workspace; defaults to /workspace.

timeoutMs.description: Execution timeout in milliseconds; defaults to 300000 and caps at 600000.

tools.name: ui_open
tools.description: Create or open an agent-made HTML app in a visible WebMCP Computer window. Pass exactly one of html or an existing ~-rooted .html path; inline HTML is written to ~/apps/ .html and remains live-editable by the human. The app runs in an opaque allow-scripts sandbox with no same-origin or popup access. Its HTML may publish site_* WebMCP tools through document.modelContext. allowTools defaults to an empty inward grant and may expose active non-transact OS tools; transact tools, site_* tools, unknown tools, and ui_open are always excluded. Returns PID, file path, applied rect, and the granted tool names.

name.description: File-safe app name used for inline HTML under ~/apps/.

html.description: Complete HTML document, up to 256 KB UTF-8; mutually exclusive with path.

path.description: Existing ~-rooted .html text file; mutually exclusive with html.

allowTools.description: OS tool names the app may call; omitted means no tools.

x.description: Optional work-area horizontal position in CSS pixels.

y.description: Optional work-area vertical position in CSS pixels.

width.description: Optional window width in CSS pixels.

height.description: Optional window height in CSS pixels.

focus.description: Whether to focus the new window; defaults to true.

tools.name: fs_read
tools.description: Read one UTF-8 text file from the shared WebMCP Computer filesystem by ~-rooted path. Text files only; content over 256 KB is truncated and `truncated: true` is set. Pass encoding="base64" to read any file as base64; oversized base64 output fails instead of being truncated.

path.description: ~-rooted file path to read.

tools.name: fs_write
tools.description: Create or replace one UTF-8 text file in the shared WebMCP Computer filesystem. Empty content truncates the file to zero bytes. Parent directory must exist; visible Files and Editor windows update live. Pass encoding="base64" to decode content and atomically write binary bytes.

path.description: ~-rooted destination file path.

content.description: Complete UTF-8 file content; empty string truncates to zero bytes.

tools.name: fs_edit
tools.description: Replace exact text in one UTF-8 file. old_string must be a unique anchor unless replace_all=true; if it matches zero or multiple times, the error tells you to choose a longer anchor. Returns the normalized path and replacement count.

path.description: ~-rooted text-file path to edit.

old_string.description: Exact existing text; unique unless replace_all is true.

replace_all.description: Replace every exact match instead of requiring one unique match.

tools.name: fs_search
tools.description: Search text-file contents case-insensitively below a ~-rooted path, skipping binary files. Returns matching path, 1-based line number, and full line text, plus a truncated flag when max_results is exceeded.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring to find.

path.description: ~-rooted file or directory; defaults to ~.

max_results.description: Maximum matches to return; defaults to 50.

tools.name: fs_list
tools.description: List direct children of one ~-rooted WebMCP Computer directory. Returns sorted directories first, then files, with type, size, and modification time.

path.description: ~-rooted directory path to list.

tools.name: fs_mkdir
tools.description: Create one directory at a ~-rooted path. Parent directory must already exist.

path.description: ~-rooted directory path to create.

tools.name: fs_delete
tools.description: Delete one file or directory tree from the shared WebMCP Computer filesystem. The home root itself cannot be deleted.

path.description: ~-rooted file or directory to delete.

tools.name: fs_move
tools.description: Move or rename one file or directory between two ~-rooted paths. Destination parent must exist and destination must be absent unless overwrite=true is passed; overwrite defaults to false.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing destination. Defaults to false.

tools.name: term_exec
tools.description: Visibly type and execute one just-bash command against the shared WebMCP Computer filesystem. Opens a Terminal when none exists; optionally target a terminal PID. Supports pipes, redirects, variables, subshells, jq, awk, sed, grep, and other bundled commands; network, Python, and JavaScript runtimes are disabled. Times out after 30s by default; timeout_ms can set up to 120s. Returns stdout, stderr, exit_code, and truncated after output appears; stdout and stderr are each capped at 256 KB.

command.description: Shell command to type and execute.

term_pid.description: Optional PID of an open Terminal window.

timeout_ms.description: Execution timeout in milliseconds; defaults to 30000 and caps at 120000.

tools.name: term_read
tools.description: Read the last lines of an open WebMCP Computer Terminal's shared 2000-line scrollback. Defaults to the frontmost Terminal and 50 lines; returns the terminal PID, plain-text lines, and truncated when older scrollback was discarded.

term_pid.description: Optional PID of an open Terminal window.

lines.description: Number of trailing lines; defaults to 50.

tools.name: term_state
tools.description: Read the live shell session behind the frontmost Terminal: PID, cwd, busy state, optional running command, and environment. Pass term_pid to target another Terminal. This reads session objects, never parsed scrollback.

term_pid.description: Optional PID of an open Terminal window.

tools.name: term_history
tools.description: Read structured command history from the live frontmost Terminal session, shared with the human and ordered oldest to newest. Defaults to 50 entries; pass term_pid to target another Terminal.

term_pid.description: Optional PID of an open Terminal window.

limit.description: Trailing history entries; defaults to 50.

tools.name: ps
tools.description: List the real WebMCP Computer process table: PID 1, open app windows, and transient running shell commands. Returns small records with PID, kind, command, and optional app or cwd.

tools.name: kill
tools.description: Terminate one WebMCP Computer app window or transient shell command by PID. PID 1 is protected. Returns the killed process record; throws when the PID does not exist.

Available warehouses (for warehouse pins): Chicago Hub (Chicago, USA, North America) at [41.88, -87.63], capacity 78%; Rotterdam Port (Rotterdam, Netherlands, Europe) at [51.92, 4.48], capacity 85%; Shanghai Terminal (Shanghai, China, Asia Pacific) at [31.23, 121.47], capacity 92%; São Paulo Center (São Paulo, Brazil, Latin America) at [-23.55, -46.63], capacity 61%; Mumbai Gateway (Mumbai, India, Asia Pacific) at [19.08, 72.88], capacity 88%; Tokyo Depot (Tokyo, Japan, Asia Pacific) at [35.68, 139.69], capacity 73%; Sydney Warehouse (Sydney, Australia, Oceania) at [-33.87, 151.21], capacity 55%; Lagos Depot (Lagos, Nigeria, Africa) at [6.52, 3.38], capacity 42% (warehouse-map map)

To populate the spreadsheet from the Shipment Tracker grid, ALWAYS first call shipment-tracker Filter (if criteria given) and then shipment-tracker GetData to retrieve the visible rows. Lat', L='Dest. Lng'; and (2) one row per shipment starting at row 2, mapping TrackingNumber→A, Origin→B, Destination→C, DestinationStreet→D, Status→E, Carrier→F, Value→G, Weight→H, ShipDate→I, ETA→J, DestinationLat→K, DestinationLng→L. tools.name: inventory-sheet-spreadsheet-rename-sheet
tools.description: Rename a sheet in the Warehouse Capacity spreadsheet. (inventory-sheet spreadsheet)

tools.name: shipment-tracker-grid-group

tools.name: shipment-tracker-grid-clear-group

sites.name: panoptik-studio.vercel.app
sites.description: Browser-native demo video editor where humans and AI agents co-edit on the same canvas via WebMCP. No uploads, no server.

tools.name: get_project_state
tools.description: MANDATORY FIRST STEP for any video editing, review, or enhancement request. Returns the full project: clips, durations, zooms, overlays, audio, plus the Director Playbook and the autonomous decision tree for vague requests like 'edit this video'. All timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds; check timelineRevision — if it changed since your last read, your cached observations are stale and you MUST re-ingest.

tools.name: list_clips
tools.description: Returns all timeline video clips with cumulative start/end timestamps, durations, speeds, and transitions. All times are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

tools.name: list_scenes
tools.description: Returns all timeline segments (scenes) with cumulative timeline start/end timestamps, duration, speed, and transitions. All times are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

tools.name: get_silence_intervals
tools.description: Detects audio silence and dead-air intervals where the speaker is inactive, returned in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. Use for ripple trimming: dead air >= 1.5s is a cut candidate ({op:'cut', dropSilence:true}). Requires transcription — call generate_captions first if status is PENDING_TRANSCRIPTION.

minDurationSec.description: Minimum silence duration threshold in seconds (default 1.0).

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Returns the spoken transcript with timestamps in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. If empty, call generate_captions to transcribe. Re-fetch this after any cut/delete/speed change — earlier timestamps go stale when the timeline shifts.

tools.name: inspect_timeline
tools.description: Detailed inspector of all clips, timeline timestamps, transitions, speed, zooms, and overlays. All times are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

tools.name: get_click_log
tools.description: Returns cursor telemetry in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. Default response is COMPACT: per-20s attention buckets (where the mouse was active), click counts, and suggested zoom timestamps — plus exact cursor (x, y) interpolation via atTimestamp. Pass detail:'full' for the raw point list (token-heavy; rarely needed). Click clusters are prime zoom candidates; a parked cursor (no recent events) is NOT a good zoom target.

atTimestamp.description: Optional: interpolate and return the exact cursor (x, y) at this timeline timestamp

detail.description: 'summary' (default) returns attention buckets only; 'full' also includes the raw point list.

tools.name: export_clip
tools.description: Renders and exports the edited video locally in the browser via WebCodecs. Prompts the human for confirmation before encoding. Returns a downloadable Blob URL and file metadata upon completion.

format.description: Video container format. 'mp4' (H.264) is most compatible; 'webm' (VP9) is smaller.

resolution.description: Export resolution. '1080p' is standard HD, '720p' is faster, '4k' is ultra high-res.

tools.name: propose_zoom_points
tools.description: Proposes zoom-in keyframes at specific timeline timestamps. Proposals appear as ghost diamond markers on the timeline for human review — they are NOT applied until commit_staged_changes. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

timestamps.description: Timeline seconds where zoom-in keyframes should be placed.

focalX.description: Normalized focal X center (0 to 1, default 0.5).

focalY.description: Normalized focal Y center (0 to 1, default 0.5).

tools.name: add_text_overlay
tools.description: Stages a styled text caption or annotation overlay at a specific timeline timestamp and screen position. Supports custom fonts, sizes, colors, backdrops, and entrance/exit animations. Staged overlays appear for review until committed. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

text.description: The text content to display (no emojis).

timestamp.description: When the text should appear (timeline seconds).

tools.name: set_background
tools.description: Stages a background color or gradient change. Fills the stage padding area around the video when aspect ratio padding is visible.

kind.description: Background type: 'solid' (single color) or 'gradient' (two-stop linear gradient).

color.description: Hex color for solid background, e.g. '#0a0a0a'.

stops.description: Array of two hex colors for gradient, e.g. ['#007cf0', '#7928ca'].

tools.name: generate_captions
tools.description: Transcribes the video's audio (camera/mic + screen tracks separately) and generates timestamped additive subtitle phrases across the timeline — same pipeline as the manual Auto-Generate button. Always call this first if get_transcript is empty — cuts, zooms and silence detection all depend on speech timestamps.

language.description: Audio language: 'auto', 'hinglish', 'en', 'hi', 'es', 'fr', 'de', 'ja', 'zh'. Default 'auto'.

includeSpeakerLabels.description: Prefix captions with 'Speaker:' / 'Screen:' (default true, matches the manual Speaker toggle).

presetId.description: Caption style preset id: viral, clean, outline, subtitles, electric, highlighter (default 'viral').

speakerFontSize.description: Font size px for Speaker captions (default 36).

screenFontSize.description: Font size px for Screen captions (default 28).

tools.name: split_clip
tools.description: Splits the clip at a timeline timestamp into two segments. Use before delete_clip to remove an unwanted range. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. The response includes the new clip map — use it, not your pre-split observations.

timestamp.description: Timeline second where the split cut should occur.

tools.name: split_segment
tools.description: Splits the video clip at the given timeline timestamp. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. The response includes the new clip map.

timestamp.description: Timeline second where the split should occur.

tools.name: delete_clip
tools.description: Deletes a clip segment and ripple-joins the adjacent clips. THIS SHIFTS THE TIMELINE: every timestamp after the deleted range moves earlier. The response flags timelineShifted — you MUST re-ingest get_project_state and get_transcript afterwards and never reuse pre-delete timestamps. Cannot delete the only remaining clip.

clipIndex.description: 0-based index of the clip segment to delete.

tools.name: set_clip_transition
tools.description: Sets the incoming transition effect and duration on a clip segment. Does not shift timestamps.

tools.name: set_clip_speed
tools.description: Sets playback speed for a clip segment (0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x, 3x with pitch-preserved WSOLA audio). THIS SHIFTS THE TIMELINE: the segment's duration changes, so later timestamps compress or expand. Re-ingest after calling.

tools.name: set_speed
tools.description: Sets playback speed multiplier for the selected segment (0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x). THIS SHIFTS THE TIMELINE — re-ingest after calling.

tools.name: set_aspect
tools.description: Sets the stage aspect ratio preset ('16:9', '9:16', '1:1', '4:3', or 'source'). Does not shift timestamps.

tools.name: add_music
tools.description: Adds or moves an audio track on the timeline at a specified start timestamp (timeline seconds).

tools.name: get_director_guidelines
tools.description: Returns the authoritative Video Director reasoning playbook: multimodal heuristics, zoom scales, text overlay rules (no emojis), keepouts, the staleness contract, and the autonomous decision tree for vague requests like 'edit the reaction video'.

tools.name: get_video_summary
tools.description: Returns the complete semantic summary of the loaded video in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds: transcript phrases, scene breakdown, silence intervals, dead air, facecam corner, and the Director Playbook. Call this to understand the video before editing; call generate_captions first if the transcript is missing.

tools.name: get_scene_detail
tools.description: Lazy drill-down: returns raw click coordinates, bounding box, and word-level timestamps for a single scene. Windows are in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

tools.name: probe_frames
tools.description: Samples video frames at timeline timestamps: returns deterministic feature summaries and base64 snapshot images with an optional A1..C3 alphanumeric 3x3 grid for visual grounding. Snapshot rendering can take seconds on long recordings — request only the timestamps you need and set includeSnapshot:false when you only need features. Use the grid cells to reference screen regions in locate_visual_target. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

timestamps.description: List of timeline timestamps to query

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to generate base64 image snapshots for visual inspection (default: true)

gridOverlay.description: Whether to overlay a 3x3 alphanumeric grid (A1..C3) on the snapshot (default: true)

tools.name: locate_visual_target
tools.description: Grounds a visual target into a safe zoom focal point via a 3-tier hierarchy: (1) click telemetry near the timestamp (confidence 1.0), (2) parse VLM output — Gemini-style 0-1000 bbox, 3x3 grid cell (A1..C3), or normalized x/y — from probe_frames snapshots, (3) fallback center with guidance. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

query.description: Target element description, e.g. 'elephant' or 'search bar'

vlmOutput.description: Raw VLM response containing bbox or grid cell (if already called)

tools.name: propose_edits
tools.description: The main editing tool: applies one atomic batch of edit ops in a single call. STAGE BASELINE (automatic): every batch applies the signature look — gradient backdrop, 28px stage padding, 16px rounded frame corners — unless the batch carries its own {op:'bg'}. ZOOMS PERSIST: zoom windows auto-extend until the next scene boundary or a sustained cursor move to a different region (minimum 4s hold). Ops (times in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds): {op:'cut', t0, t1} removes the exact window — the deterministic form, pass the intervals from get_silence_intervals; {op:'cut', t, dropSilence:true} expands t to the matching silence interval; a cut without a window or matching silence is REJECTED, never silently skipped. Also: {op:'zoom', t0, t1, cx?, cy?, scale?, ease?}; {op:'text', t, text, pos?:'top'|'bottom'|'center', dur?, fontSize?, fontWeight?, color?, backgroundColor?, animation?}; {op:'cam', corner:'tl'|'tr'|'bl'|'br', shape?, size?}; {op:'bg', kind:'solid'|'gradient', c0, c1?}; {op:'trans', at, kind, dur?}; {op:'speed', t0, t1, mult}. mode 'replace' clears prior agent zooms/overlays but NEVER Whisper captions. MANDATORY RULES: (1) NO emojis in text. (2) Multi-stage sequential pans (1.6x-1.8x) for long content. (3) Invert overlay position vs zoom half. (4) Verify targets via probe_frames, not a parked cursor. AFTER CUTS: the response sets cutsApplied and timelineShifted — re-ingest get_project_state + get_transcript before any further op batch. CHECK rejectedOps: a rejected cut means dead air was NOT removed.

ops.description: Array of EditOp objects (see description for the exact shapes)

plan.description: Concise explanation of your editorial strategy

mode.description: replace (default) or append

tools.name: commit_staged_changes
tools.description: Commits ALL staged ghost proposals (from propose_zoom_points, add_text_overlay, set_background, generate_captions) permanently. Shows the staged diff dialog for human confirmation. Edits already applied via propose_edits need no commit.

tools.name: discard_staged_changes
tools.description: Clears all pending ghost edit proposals without modifying the committed project.

tools.name: cloud_transcribe
tools.description: Transcribes project audio using Cloud Whisper Large v3 with word timestamps (Requires Pro or BYOK). Prefer generate_captions first — it both transcribes and stages caption overlays.

language.description: Optional ISO language code (e.g. 'en')

tools.name: ai_auto_director
tools.description: Hosted 1-click auto-director: sends the video digest to a cloud model (Claude Haiku / Gemini Flash) which returns a full edit plan, applied via the same snapping pipeline as propose_edits (Requires Pro or BYOK). Air-gapped mode blocks it — use the local tool pipeline instead.

text.description: The draft text to review.

criteria.description: Review criteria to check against (e.g. 'grammatical correctness', 'consistent use of past tense', 'no unsupported factual claims').

sites.name: fieldwork-beat-machine.openai.chatgpt.site
sites.description: A tactile 12-voice beat machine with classic drum-machine grooves, deep synths, keyboard and touch pads, WebMCP controls, and stereo WAV export.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Read the current beat-machine preset, tempo, transport, musical key and scale, 24-sound library, six editable instrument slots and their complete sound-design parameters, selected pad bank, all 12 playable pads, plus the 12 by 16 velocity and MIDI-note patterns.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Read the complete portable Fieldwork project document, including its name, pattern, notes, mix, musical key, and six instrument patches. Use it for backup or as input to load_project.

tools.name: load_project
tools.description: Validate and atomically replace the current local project with a Fieldwork project document. Stops playback and recording, preserves an undo step, and autosaves locally. Invalid documents leave the current project unchanged.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Create a portable JSON backup of the current project and optionally download it. This does not render audio; use export_track for WAV audio.

tools.name: undo_edit
tools.description: Undo the most recent local project edit. Returns changed=false when no undo history remains.

tools.name: redo_edit
tools.description: Restore the most recently undone local project edit. Returns changed=false when no redo history remains.

tools.name: set_tempo
tools.description: Set the beat-machine tempo in BPM (45 to 220).

tools.name: set_swing
tools.description: Set sixteenth-note swing. Use a fraction from 0 to 0.45 or a percentage from 0 to 45.

tools.name: set_controls
tools.description: Adjust the beat-machine mix and timing controls: tempo, swing, tone, space, master volume, humanize, and default export bars. Omitted controls stay unchanged.

tools.name: select_kit
tools.description: Load one of the nine instrument and groove presets: 808-night, 909-warehouse, linn-pop, sp-dust, mpc-swing, acid-cell, electro-break, dub-orbit, or minimal-12.

tools.name: select_instrument
tools.description: Map the performance pads to all voices, a 12-pad drum bank, or one of six playable instrument slots using the selected key and scale. Slots are laid out U I O / J K L; instruments can be lead, chord, pluck, bass, sub, or tuned fx.

tools.name: configure_instrument
tools.description: Load one of 24 categorized sound presets into a U I O / J K L instrument slot, or target a base voice. Sounds cover neon leads, pads, brass, strings, keys, bells, acid, reese, 808 and sub basses, noise, radio, and atmospheric FX.

tools.name: configure_instruments
tools.description: Atomically load sounds into 1 to 6 distinct U I O / J K L instrument slots. Results preserve input order; duplicate slots or any invalid item reject the whole batch without changing the current configuration.

tools.name: set_instrument_params
tools.description: Dial in an instrument slot with attack, decay, sustain, release, cutoff, resonance, drive, motion, stereo width, octave, and waveform. Omitted sound-design controls stay unchanged and changes apply to live playback and WAV export.

tools.name: reset_instrument
tools.description: Restore a U I O / J K L instrument slot's current sound preset to its original ADSR, filter, drive, motion, width, octave, and waveform settings.

tools.name: randomize_instrument
tools.description: Create a playable sound-design variation for a U I O / J K L instrument slot. An optional seed makes the ADSR, filter, motion, waveform, and timbre result repeatable.

tools.name: set_key
tools.description: Choose the musical root and scale used by all twelve melodic pads. Root accepts note names such as C, F#, Bb, or a pitch class from 0 to 11; scales are minor, major, dorian, pentatonic, and chromatic.

tools.name: set_step
tools.description: Write or clear a single sequencer step, optionally setting a MIDI note for a melodic lane. Steps are numbered 1 to 16; voices include kick, snare, clap, hatClosed, hatOpen, perc, sub, bass, chord, lead, pluck, and fx.

tools.name: set_pattern
tools.description: Replace any number of voice lanes in the 16-step sequencer. Supply velocity lanes and, optionally, matching MIDI-note lanes to lay complete melodic tracks in one action; omitted lanes stay unchanged.

tools.name: clear_pattern
tools.description: Clear all 12 sequencer lanes, leaving a silent 16-step grid ready for an agent or performer to lay a new track.

tools.name: set_voice_mute
tools.description: Mute or unmute one instrument lane without deleting its sequencer steps.

tools.name: set_recording
tools.description: Arm or disarm on-tempo grid recording. When armed, performance pads and trigger-pad actions can print at the playhead.

tools.name: mutate_pattern
tools.description: Create a musical variation or fill while keeping the core kick and sub pocket intact.

tools.name: transport
tools.description: Start, stop, or toggle the beat-machine transport.

tools.name: trigger_pad
tools.description: Audition a voice or one of the 12 currently mapped performance pads and optionally place it onto the current sequencer step. Melodic pads automatically print their note; an explicit MIDI note can override it.

tools.name: export_track
tools.description: Render the current beat and synth arrangement to a stereo 48 kHz WAV file, make it available for preview, and optionally download it.

currency.description: Authoritative 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. USD, NGN)

appliedCoupon.description: Applied promotional coupon code or null

expiresAt.description: ISO timestamp when the 15-minute price lock expires

requiresPaymentAuthorization.description: Always true: order requires explicit customer confirmation

error.description: Error message if checkout cannot be prepared

confirmed.description: Set to true after the customer confirms the order total.

confirmationId.description: Optional confirmation tracking token or receipt reference.

success.description: Whether the order was successfully accepted

currency.description: Authoritative 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. USD, NGN)

error.description: Error reason if order was rejected

tools.name: request_staff
