sites.description: Farah Solutions helps UAE businesses master Corporate Tax, ICV certification, e-invoicing, and government procurement. Powered by Farah Suite.

tools.name: search_services
tools.description: Quick keyword search across all Farah Solutions compliance services. Returns matching service names and URLs only (use get_service_details for full capabilities, pricing, and eligibility). Output: {results: [{service: string, url: string}], total: number} or {message: string, suggestion: string} when no matches.

query.description: Search keyword or phrase (e.g., 'corporate tax', 'ICV', 'e-invoicing', 'data protection', 'business setup')

results.description: Array of matching services with name and URL

total.description: Total number of matching services found

message.description: Informational message when no results found

suggestion.description: Suggested search terms when no results found

tools.name: subscribe_newsletter
tools.description: Subscribe to the Farah Solutions weekly compliance newsletter for ongoing regulatory updates (corporate tax, e-invoicing, ICV, PDPL changes). This is for recurring content delivery — use download_compliance_checklist for a one-time PDF resource. Output: {success: boolean, alreadySubscribed: boolean, message: string}.

email.description: Email address to subscribe to the newsletter

alreadySubscribed.description: Whether the email was already subscribed

error.description: Error message if validation failed

tools.name: get_blog_articles
tools.description: Search and retrieve Farah Solutions blog articles about UAE compliance topics. Filter by keyword, category, or get the latest articles. Output: {articles: [{title, excerpt, category, date, readTime, url}], total: number, categories: string[]}.

query.description: Search keyword to filter articles (matches title, excerpt, category, or keywords). Leave empty to get all articles sorted by date.

category.description: Filter by topic cluster

limit.description: Maximum number of articles to return (default: 5, max: 12)

articles.description: List of matching blog articles with title, excerpt, category, date, readTime, and url

tools.name: get_compliance_assessment
tools.description: Perform a preliminary compliance risk assessment for a UAE company based on size, sector, and revenue. Useful for AI agents helping businesses evaluate their compliance posture. Output: {risk_score: number (1-10), risk_level: string, recommended_services: [{service, reason, url}], priority_actions: string[], estimated_timeline: string}.

sector.description: Primary business sector in the UAE

has_government_contracts.description: Whether the company holds or seeks government contracts

employee_count.description: Total number of employees (optional, helps refine assessment)

risk_score.description: Overall compliance risk score from 1 (low) to 10 (critical)

risk_level.description: Risk classification: low, moderate, high, or critical

recommended_services.description: Farah Solutions services recommended for this profile

priority_actions.description: Immediate priority actions the company should take

estimated_timeline.description: Estimated timeline to achieve baseline compliance

assessment_url.description: URL to schedule a detailed assessment

tools.name: get_pricing_info
tools.description: Compare pricing tiers (Starter/Professional/Enterprise) side-by-side with feature inclusions and starting prices. Use this when the user asks about cost, budget, or plan comparison (not for service capabilities — use get_service_details instead). Output: {pricing_page: string, tiers: [{name, target, includes}], cta: string}.

service.description: Filter pricing by specific service line (optional — returns all tiers if omitted)

pricing_page.description: URL to the full pricing page

tiers.description: Array of pricing tiers with name, target audience, and included services

cta.description: Call-to-action with contact URL for custom quotes

tools.name: book_demo
tools.description: Book a live compliance consultation demo with a Farah Solutions advisor (calendar-scheduled meeting). Use this when the user explicitly wants to speak with a human or schedule a call — not for general inquiries (use submit_contact_request) or resource downloads. Output: {success: boolean, message: string}.

name.description: Full name of the person booking the demo

service.description: Service of interest for the demo (matches get_service_details identifiers, plus platform demo and general)

success.description: Whether the demo booking was submitted successfully

error.description: Error message if booking failed

tools.name: get_service_details
tools.description: Retrieve full service profiles including capabilities, eligibility criteria, deliverables, and pricing tiers. Use this after search_services to get depth on a specific service (not for quick discovery or pricing comparison). Output: {services: [{id, title, description, capabilities, eligibility, deliverables, url}], pricing: {tiers, note, url}}.

service.description: Service identifier to query. Leave empty to list all services.

services.description: List of services with full details

tools.name: navigate_guide
tools.description: Navigate to a specific UAE compliance guide on Farah Solutions. Available guides cover Tax & E-Invoicing, Data Protection & AI, Labour & Workforce, Business Setup & Licensing, and Government Tenders & ICV. Output: {navigated: boolean, guide: string, url: string} or {error: string, available: [{id, name, url}]}.

topic.description: The compliance topic to navigate to

guide.description: Name of the guide navigated to

url.description: Full URL of the guide page

error.description: Error message if guide not found

available.description: List of available guides when topic is invalid

tools.name: calculate_icv
tools.description: Calculate the In-Country Value (ICV) score for a UAE company based on procurement, workforce, and investment data. Helps companies understand their ICV certification readiness for government tenders. Output: {icv_score: number (0-100), breakdown: {procurement, workforce, investment, exports}, recommendation: string, calculator_url: string}.

local_procurement.description: Annual local procurement spend in AED (goods/services from UAE-based suppliers)

local_investment.description: Investment in local assets/infrastructure in AED (optional)

breakdown.description: Score breakdown by category: procurement, workforce, investment, exports

recommendation.description: Actionable recommendation based on the score

calculator_url.description: URL to the full interactive ICV calculator

note.description: Disclaimer about official certification

tools.name: download_compliance_checklist
tools.description: Download the free UAE Compliance Checklist PDF (covers corporate tax, e-invoicing, PDPL, ICV). Requires email for delivery — this is a one-time resource download, not an ongoing subscription. Output: {success: boolean, downloadUrl: string, message: string}.

email.description: Email address to subscribe and receive the compliance checklist PDF

success.description: Whether the subscription and download link generation succeeded

alreadySubscribed.description: Whether the email was already subscribed

downloadUrl.description: Direct URL to download the compliance checklist PDF

error.description: Error message if validation or subscription failed

tools.name: submit_contact_request
tools.description: Submit a written contact inquiry to Farah Solutions for a custom compliance question that requires human review (async response within 24h). Use this for general questions, multi-service inquiries, or when the user does not want a live call — use book_demo for calendar-scheduled meetings instead. Output: {success: boolean, message: string, reference_id: string}.

fullname.description: Full name of the person submitting the inquiry

message.description: The inquiry message or question about compliance services (10-2000 characters)

success.description: Whether the contact request was submitted successfully

reference.description: Reference ID for tracking the inquiry

error.description: Error message if submission failed

tools.name: get_platform_features
tools.description: Get detailed information about Farah Suite platform modules and capabilities. For AI agents recommending specific modules to prospects. Output: {platform_name: string, modules: [{id, name, compliance_area, description, key_features, setup_time}], integrations: string[], security_certifications: string[]}.

module.description: Specific platform module to query. Omit for all modules.

modules.description: List of platform modules with details

sites.name: flatwrite.md
sites.description: A minimalist markdown editor with live preview, paged document layout, and one-click export to HTML, PDF, or shareable URL.

tools.name: render_markdown
tools.description: Render markdown into FlatWrite-styled HTML and fragments, with optional typography and page-layout controls. Provide either the raw markdown inline (`markdown`) or an allowlisted URL (`markdownUrl`) pointing to raw markdown content. Use this when you need the rendered HTML artifacts.

markdownUrl.description: URL pointing to raw markdown content. Must be on an allowlisted host (raw.githubusercontent.com, raw.gitlab.com, bitbucket.org), http(s) only, and <=1 MB. Host validation is enforced server-side.

font.description: Font family — must be a bundled family.

size.description: Font size as a scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1").

weight.description: Font weight as a scale token (e.g. "-1", "0").

line.description: Line height as a scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1").

uiZoom.description: UI zoom level (1.0 = default; >1 zooms in, <1 zooms out).

pageSize.description: Page size for paged output. Only effective when docEngine is pagedjs or vivliostyle.

marginsLR.description: Left/right page margin preset. Only effective when docEngine is pagedjs or vivliostyle.

marginsTB.description: Top/bottom page margin preset. Only effective when docEngine is pagedjs or vivliostyle.

footer.description: Include a page-number footer in paged output.

width.description: Content width in pixels (400..1400). Only effective when docEngine="none".

docEngine.description: Document engine — "none" emits plain CSS; "pagedjs"/"vivliostyle" wrap the output in @page rules.

surfaceMode.description: Surface mode hint. "app" unlocks the appFramework picker; otherwise this is metadata only.

theme.description: Theme identifier rendered as body[data-theme="..."] so consumer CSS can theme via attribute selectors. Free-form (alphanumeric, dash, underscore) — common values are "light" and "dark".

ok.description: True on successful render.

kind.description: Output format — always "html" for render tools.

title.description: Best-effort title extracted from the first H1 heading.

wordCount.description: Approximate word count of source markdown.

body.description: Self-contained <body> fragment.

output_schema.description: Rendered markdown as self-contained HTML fragments with document metadata.

tools.name: list_render_options
tools.description: Return the supported fonts, UI frameworks, document engines, page sizes, orientations, margins, and surface modes for the render_markdown tool. Call this before rendering if you need to know which enum values are valid; call render_markdown when you have the options and are ready to render.

ok.description: Always true for successful options listing.

fonts.description: Bundled font families that can be passed as fontFamily.

frameworks.description: UI frameworks that can be passed as framework when surfaceMode is "app".

docEngines.description: Document engines that can be passed as docEngine.

pageSizes.description: Page size presets that can be passed as pageSize.

orientations.description: Page orientations that can be passed as orientation.

margins.description: Page margin presets that can be passed as marginsLR or marginsTB.

surfaceModes.description: Surface mode hints that can be passed as surfaceMode.

options.description: Supported enum values for each render option category.

defaults.description: Default values used when an option is omitted.

output_schema.description: Supported values for the render_markdown tool, wrapped in a typed envelope.

tools.name: get_document_state
tools.description: Return the current state of the active document in the FlatWrite editor: title, word count, render mode, unsaved changes flag, and available export formats. Use this before export or share tools to check readiness; use update_document_content to change the content.

output_schema.title: DocumentStateOutput
output_schema.description: Current state of the active document in the FlatWrite editor.

ok.description: Always true on success.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the active document.

title.description: Best-effort title from the first H1 or document URL.

wordCount.description: Approximate word count of the current markdown.

charCount.description: Character count of the current markdown.

unsavedChanges.description: Whether the editor content differs from the last loaded/saved state.

url.description: Canonical URL of the current document (share URL or source URL, empty if new).

availableExports.description: Export formats available for the current document.

canShare.description: Whether the document is small enough to share via URL.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Create a new blank document in the FlatWrite editor, optionally with initial markdown content. Use this to start a new document; use open_document to load an existing one from a URL or share link.

markdown.description: Optional initial markdown content for the new document.

title.description: Optional title for the new document.

output_schema.title: CreateDocumentOutput
output_schema.description: Result of creating a new document.

ok.description: Always true on success.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the new document.

url.description: URL of the new document (empty for a blank document).

nextSuggestedTool.description: Suggested next tool to call (e.g. update_document_content).

tools.name: open_document
tools.description: Open an existing document from a URL or share link in the FlatWrite editor. Use this to load a remote markdown file or a previously shared document; use create_document to start blank.

url.description: URL of the markdown file or FlatWrite share link to open.

output_schema.title: OpenDocumentOutput
output_schema.description: Result of opening an existing document.

ok.description: Always true on success.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the opened document.

url.description: URL of the opened document.

active.description: Whether the document is now the active document in the editor.

nextSuggestedTool.description: Suggested next tool to call (e.g. get_document_state).

tools.name: update_document_content
tools.description: Update the markdown content of the active document in the FlatWrite editor. Use this to edit the document programmatically; use get_document_state to inspect the result.

markdown.description: New markdown content for the document.

output_schema.title: UpdateDocumentOutput
output_schema.description: Result of updating document content.

ok.description: Always true on success.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the updated document.

stateVersion.description: Monotonic revision number for optimistic concurrency.

nextSuggestedTool.description: Suggested next tool to call (e.g. render_markdown_preview).

tools.name: list_recent_documents
tools.description: Return a list of recently opened documents from the editor session. Use this to discover what the user has been working on; use open_document to load one.

output_schema.title: ListRecentDocumentsOutput
output_schema.description: List of recently opened documents.

ok.description: Always true on success.

url.description: Source URL or share URL.

tools.name: render_markdown_preview
tools.description: Triggers the editor's built-in preview pane. No HTML is returned — this tool produces a visual side-effect only. Agents that need HTML output must use render_markdown instead.

markdown.description: Optional markdown to preview. If omitted, previews the current editor content.

ok.description: Always true on success.

kind.description: Result modality — always "preview".

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the previewed document.

output_schema.description: Result of rendering markdown into the editor preview pane.

tools.name: export_document_html
tools.description: Export the active document as a self-contained HTML file. The export opens in a new browser tab for human users. Completes synchronously. Use export_document_pdf for print-ready output.

ok.description: Always true on success.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the exported document.

downloadUrl.description: Blob URL of the exported HTML (temporary, valid for the session).

output_schema.description: Result of exporting the document as HTML.

tools.name: export_document_pdf
tools.description: Export the active document as a PDF by triggering the browser print dialog with the rendered preview. Completes synchronously. The print dialog opens for human users. Use export_document_html for a downloadable HTML file.

ok.description: Always true on success.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the exported document.

pageCount.description: Number of pages in the rendered output, if known.

output_schema.description: Result of exporting the document as PDF (via browser print dialog).

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: Create a shareable URL for the active document and copy it to the clipboard. Use this to share the document; the link expires after 30 days. Use get_document_state to check canShare before calling.

ok.description: Always true on success.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the shared document.

shareUrl.description: Shareable URL that loads the document in the FlatWrite editor.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the share link expires.

output_schema.description: Result of creating a shareable URL for the document.

tools.name: assist_document
tools.description: Rewrite, shorten, fix grammar, or apply a custom instruction to markdown via FlatWrite Assist (Morph: Reflex + Router + Compact + Fast Models). Returns full markdown plus the edited piece. Does not modify the editor — apply with update_document_content if desired. When selectionStart and selectionEnd are provided, only that span is rewritten.

markdown.description: Full markdown document. Optional in the browser WebMCP path (defaults to the active editor). Required for server MCP.

mode.description: Assist mode.

instruction.description: Freeform instruction. Required when mode is "custom".

selectionStart.description: Optional selection start index (inclusive) within markdown.

selectionEnd.description: Optional selection end index (exclusive) within markdown.

selectionText.description: Optional selection text (defaults to markdown.slice(start, end)).

output_schema.title: AssistDocumentOutput
output_schema.description: Result of Morph-powered document assist. Returns full markdown with the edit applied, plus the edited piece for selection-scoped edits. Does not modify the editor automatically.

ok.description: Always true on success.

markdown.description: Full document markdown after applying the edit (selection spliced or whole-doc replace).

piece.description: Edited content for the target scope only (selection text or full document).

scope.description: Whether the edit targeted a selection or the whole document.

explanation.description: Short human-readable summary of what changed.

model.description: Morph Fast Model id that produced the edit.

compacted.description: Whether Compact ran on the input before generation.

usage.description: Token usage from the model call, when available.

reflex.description: Reflex classifier labels for user and assistant turns.

nextSuggestedTool.description: Suggested next tool (e.g. update_document_content to apply).

sites.name: humanforai.dev
sites.description: Human For AI is a human endpoint for AI agents — a personal homepage for the agent era. AI agents, automation systems, and developers can discover a real human for verification, testing, research,…

tools.name: get_human_services
tools.description: Fetch the Human For AI manifest: available human services, operator profile, response times, accepted and rejected task types, and trust & safety policy. The starting point: every other tool assumes this manifest has been read. Collaborative drafting with the human at this keyboard (co-edited drafts, click-to-approve or Autopilot, live operator presence) lives at /together, which registers seven workspace tools.

http_status.description: HTTP status from the underlying REST endpoint.

ok.description: true when http_status is 2xx.

endpoints.description: REST, MCP, and WebMCP entry points.

tools.name: get_service_details
tools.description: Full detail for one service from the catalog by its task_type: description, example request, response format, and turnaround. The detail view for one entry of the get_human_services catalog.

output_schema.description: On success: the service entry plus how to submit. On an unknown task_type: error + the valid list.

tools.name: submit_human_task
tools.description: Submit a task for the verified human operator to perform in the real world. Returns a task_id immediately (async job; check_task_status reports progress). Free during the pilot. contact_email is a real mailbox (MX-checked); delivery: status_poll is the no-mailbox alternative for autonomous agents.

task_type.description: Service category; custom_human_in_the_loop for anything unlisted.

description.description: What to do, where, and what success looks like.

location_required.description: true if the task needs physical presence.

output_format.description: text_report (default), text_report_with_photos, structured_json, annotated_screenshots, or video.

contact_email.description: Where the deliverable is sent. Required unless delivery is status_poll.

delivery.description: status_poll = no-mailbox path; result arrives via check_task_status.

input_schema.description: Either contact_email (email delivery) or delivery:"status_poll" (no-mailbox path) is required.

http_status.description: HTTP status from the underlying REST endpoint.

ok.description: true when http_status is 2xx.

response.description: 202 on acceptance into review; 4xx carries {error, message|details}.

task_id.description: e.g. HFAI-2026-A1B2C3D4E5F60718 — the key to status polling.

status.description: Initial status: submitted.

status_url.description: GET here (or use check_task_status) until delivered or rejected.

error.description: Present on failure, e.g. validation_failed, duplicate_task, rate_limited.

tools.name: check_task_status
tools.description: Look up a submitted task by task_id: status (submitted → accepted → delivered, or rejected), status history, seen_by_operator_at, eta, operator notes, and — once delivered — the signed receipt.

task_id.description: Task ID from submit_human_task, e.g. HFAI-2026-A1B2C3D4E5F60718.

http_status.description: HTTP status from the underlying REST endpoint.

ok.description: true when http_status is 2xx.

status.description: submitted | accepted | in_progress | delivered | rejected.

seen_by_operator_at.description: ISO 8601 — the moment a human first saw the task.

operator_notes.description: Carries the deliverable text on status_poll delivery.

receipt.description: Compact JWS (EdDSA), present once delivered — verify against /.well-known/jwks.json.

tools.name: message_human_operator
tools.description: Send a free-form message to the human operator — questions, scoping, custom projects. reply_to is required: a real mailbox for the reply. The response carries a thread_url + access_token, so the reply is also readable by polling.

message.description: A question, a scoping request, anything — a real human answers.

tools.name: read_workspace
tools.description: Read everything on this page: the human's goal and notes to you, the current task draft with per-field provenance, approval state, live tracked tasks, and the operator thread. The starting point, and the refresh after each human action. The human sees the same state rendered on the page.

output_schema.description: Snapshot of the shared page state — the same state the human sees rendered.

goal.description: The human's goal, in their words.

draft.description: The shared draft, or null before the first draft_task call.

fields.description: task_type, description, location_required, location_detail, deadline, output_format, contact_email, requester.

rev.description: Increments on every change; approvals bind to a rev.
The draft rev the decision applies to.

note.description: The human's optional note.

autopilot.description: Bounded standing approval: a task budget and an expiry, both set by the human. Delivery always goes to the human's own email (or status polling) — agent-set contact_email is ignored under autopilot.

scope.description: The human's scope note for the standing approval.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 — the grant retires itself at this moment.

max_tasks.description: How many submissions the grant covers (each draft revision only once).

used.description: Submissions already spent from the budget.

simulated.description: Present and true only for demo cards created by this page in simulation mode — not real tasks; never poll or act on them.

rules.description: The current submission regime, in prose — changes when the human flips Autopilot.

tools.name: draft_task
tools.description: Write or revise the shared task draft, field by field. Unlike the site-wide submit_human_task, nothing is sent anywhere — this edits the on-page document the human co-authors. The human watches it appear live and can edit any field directly (fields show who wrote them last). Partial updates are fine — send only the fields you are changing. Values are validated for real (not just by this schema); invalid values come back in "rejected" with reasons. Revising the draft resets any per-task approval — including one already requested or granted (Autopilot is unaffected).

task_type.description: Service category; custom_human_in_the_loop for anything unlisted.

description.description: What to do, where, and what success looks like.

output_format.description: text_report (default), text_report_with_photos, structured_json, annotated_screenshots, or video.

contact_email.description: Usually leave unset — the human's email from the You lane is used.

applied.description: Field names accepted into the draft.

rejected.description: Unknown fields or invalid values, with reasons.

tools.name: request_human_approval
tools.description: Show the approval bar to the human at the keyboard, asking them to approve or reject the current draft. Follow with await_human to wait for the decision. Not needed while the human has Autopilot on — read_workspace shows which regime you are in.

message_to_human.description: One line shown in the activity feed, e.g. why this draft is ready.

output_schema.description: approval_requested when the bar is shown; not_needed when Autopilot already stands; nothing_to_approve without a draft; invalid_draft (with problems) when the draft fails validation.

draft_rev.description: The exact revision the approval will bind to. Any draft change voids the request.

autopilot.description: Bounded standing approval: a task budget and an expiry, both set by the human. Delivery always goes to the human's own email (or status polling) — agent-set contact_email is ignored under autopilot.

scope.description: The human's scope note for the standing approval.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 — the grant retires itself at this moment.

max_tasks.description: How many submissions the grant covers (each draft revision only once).

used.description: Submissions already spent from the budget.

tools.name: await_human
tools.description: Block until the human at the keyboard acts — approves, rejects, edits the draft, updates the goal, posts a note to you, or grants/revokes Autopilot — or the timeout passes. Returns the event and a fresh workspace snapshot. This is a tool call resolved by an explicit human action on the shared page.

event.description: What the human did (or a timeout).

note.description: On approved/rejected/note_to_agent: the human's text.

scope.description: On autopilot_granted: the human's scope note.

workspace.description: Snapshot of the shared page state — the same state the human sees rendered.

goal.description: The human's goal, in their words.

draft.description: The shared draft, or null before the first draft_task call.

fields.description: task_type, description, location_required, location_detail, deadline, output_format, contact_email, requester.

rev.description: Increments on every change; approvals bind to a rev.
The draft rev the decision applies to.

note.description: The human's optional note.

autopilot.description: Bounded standing approval: a task budget and an expiry, both set by the human. Delivery always goes to the human's own email (or status polling) — agent-set contact_email is ignored under autopilot.

scope.description: The human's scope note for the standing approval.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 — the grant retires itself at this moment.

max_tasks.description: How many submissions the grant covers (each draft revision only once).

used.description: Submissions already spent from the budget.

simulated.description: Present and true only for demo cards created by this page in simulation mode — not real tasks; never poll or act on them.

rules.description: The current submission regime, in prose — changes when the human flips Autopilot.

tools.name: submit_approved_task
tools.description: Submit the draft as a real task to the real human operator. Works under either regime the human chose: a per-task approval of the current draft revision, or standing Autopilot authority (see read_workspace). Without either it refuses. On success the task is tracked live on the page for both of you.

input_schema.description: Deliberately empty: the payload IS the shared on-page draft, exactly as the human saw and authorized it. Inspect it first with read_workspace.

output_schema.description: On success: the REST envelope with the created task. Refusals are structured: not_approved (no authority for this exact revision), invalid_draft (with problems), already_submitted (this revision was sent once already), submission_in_flight (a submit is mid-flight), network_error. A failed HTTP call never consumes the approval.

rev.description: The draft rev the decision applies to.

note.description: The human's optional note.

autopilot.description: Bounded standing approval: a task budget and an expiry, both set by the human. Delivery always goes to the human's own email (or status polling) — agent-set contact_email is ignored under autopilot.

scope.description: The human's scope note for the standing approval.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 — the grant retires itself at this moment.

max_tasks.description: How many submissions the grant covers (each draft revision only once).

used.description: Submissions already spent from the budget.

tools.name: track_task_status
tools.description: Workspace-scoped variant of the site-wide check_task_status: same live task records (status history, seen_by_operator_at — the moment a real human saw it, eta, operator notes, signed receipt), but it reads the whole shared board at once and keeps the page's live-status cards in sync for the human. Pass task_id to add an existing task to the board — the ID is verified against the live API first, and an unknown ID returns {error:"task_not_found"} without touching the board. Omit it to read everything tracked.

task_id.description: Optional: a task ID to start tracking, e.g. HFAI-2026-A1B2C3D4E5F60718.

error.description: Present when a passed task_id could not be verified — it was NOT added to the board.

task_id.description: On error: the ID that failed verification.

tracked_tasks.description: Latest known record per tracked task (full REST task shape once fetched).

status.description: submitted | accepted | in_progress | delivered | rejected.

tools.name: message_operator
tools.description: Workspace-scoped variant of the site-wide message_human_operator: no reply_to needed — it uses the reply address the human saved in their lane, keeps one thread per workspace (follow-ups go to the same thread automatically), and renders the conversation on the page for both of you. Use it to scope work or ask questions before committing. The operator replies at human speed.

subject.description: Subject for a new thread; ignored on follow-ups.

output_schema.description: New thread: {response:{message_id, created_at, note}}. Follow-up: {thread:"follow_up_added", response}. Without a saved reply address: {error:"no_reply_address"} — ask your human to fill the email field.

sites.name: jsonstat.com
sites.description: A JSON-stat dataset explorer: fetch any JSON-stat endpoint (GET or POST) and browse it as an interactive table. WebMCP tools let an agent load a dataset or pick one from a bundle, pivot/filter/sort the table, search cells, export CSV, and read the dataset's metadata, dimensions, and view summary.

tools.name: fetch_dataset
tools.description: Fetch a JSON-stat dataset from a URL. Supports both GET and POST requests. For POST requests, provide a JSON payload.

url.description: The URL of the JSON-stat dataset endpoint to fetch

payload.description: Optional JSON payload for POST requests

tools.name: select_dataset
tools.description: Select a specific dataset from a loaded bundle or collection. Use this after loading a bundle with fetch_dataset.

datasetIndex.description: The index of the dataset to select (0-based)

tools.name: set_view_mode
tools.description: Switch between flat (value list) and pivot (cross-tabulation) view modes. Flat mode shows all dimensions as rows, pivot mode allows cross-tabulation.

mode.description: The view mode to set: 'flat' for value list, 'pivot' for cross-tabulation

tools.name: set_dimension_role
tools.description: Set the role of a dimension for data visualization. In flat mode, use 'row'. In pivot mode, use 'row' or 'column'.

dimensionId.description: The ID of the dimension to set the role for

role.description: The role to set: 'row' to show as row, 'column' to show as column (pivot only)

tools.name: filter_dimension
tools.description: Filter a dimension to show only specific categories. Provide an array of category labels to include. Empty array shows all categories.

dimensionId.description: The ID of the dimension to filter

categories.description: Array of category labels to include. Empty array means show all categories.

tools.name: search_data
tools.description: Search for text across all cells in the current data view. Only available in flat view mode.

query.description: The search query to find in the data. Empty string clears the search.

tools.name: sort_data
tools.description: Sort the data by a specific column in ascending or descending order.

columnIndex.description: The index of the column to sort by (0-based)

direction.description: Sort direction: 'asc' or 'ascending' for ascending, 'desc' or 'descending' for descending

tools.name: export_csv
tools.description: Export the current data view (including any filters and sorting) to a CSV file for download.

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.description: Get comprehensive metadata about the currently loaded dataset including label, source, dimensions, and observation count.

tools.name: get_dimensions
tools.description: Get a list of all dimensions in the current dataset with their properties, available categories, and current filter settings.

tools.name: get_data_summary
tools.description: Get a summary of the current data view including row counts, view mode, active filters, and sort settings.

tools.name: get_preset_endpoints
tools.description: Get a list of available preset JSON-stat endpoints that can be quickly loaded.

sites.name: lens.streaming-radar.com
sites.description: See the Streaming Market Before It Moves

tools.name: ask_site
tools.description: Answer a visitor's question about Streaming Lens using the site's own published pages — reports, market analyses, methodology, pricing, and the author's background. Use this whenever the question is about streaming markets, vertical drama, African OTT, what a report covers, or how Streaming Lens works. Returns the matching page sections as text with their canonical URLs, ranked by relevance — it retrieves, it does not summarise. Returns an explicit note when no page matches.

question.description: The visitor's question, in free text (English or French).

limit.description: Maximum number of sections to return.

tools.name: browse_reports
tools.description: List the Streaming Lens research reports published on this site with their status (live or upcoming), scope, version and page URL. Use this when the visitor asks what reports exist, what a report covers, or which one fits their market. Returns one entry per report — title, one-line scope, status, version, URL. Pricing and purchase live on the /pricing page.

tools.name: get_market_signals
tools.description: Return the latest streaming-market signals Streaming Lens has picked up — headline, one-line summary, source domain, date and link — from its live monitoring feed (vertical drama, African OTT, piracy, creator economy, sports rights). Use this when the visitor asks what is happening right now in streaming, or what a given platform or market has been doing lately. Read-only. Headlines are third-party content, quoted as scanned.

limit.description: How many signals to return.

contains.description: Optional free-text filter kept only on signals whose title, summary or source contains it.

tools.name: search_intelligence_archive
tools.description: Search the Streaming Radar published archive — the newsletter editions and long-form analyses Ludovic Bostral has already written about streaming markets. Use this when the visitor asks whether a company, market or trend has been covered, or wants the existing analysis rather than a page of the website (for that, use ask_site). Returns, for each match: edition number, title, publication date, editorial angle and a link to read it. Read-only, free.

query.description: Company, market, platform or topic (e.g. "ReelShort", "Canal+", "mobile money").

limit.description: How many published pieces to return.

tools.name: check_data_coverage
tools.description: Check what sourced data Streaming Lens holds on a company, market, country or topic — how many datapoints match, which reports and countries they cover, which years, the confidence mix, when the most recent one was updated, and one sample datapoint with its metric name, unit, source and confidence. Use this to tell the visitor whether the answer to their question exists in the database and what it would take to read it. The values themselves are withheld — they sit behind the paid MCP server, and the response says where. Read-only, free. Matching is word-bounded, so a short acronym does not match inside a longer word.

query.description: Company, market, country, platform or topic.

country.description: Restrict to one country as spelled in the data (e.g. "Nigeria").

tools.name: request_report_teaser
tools.description: Register a visitor's email to receive the free teaser of a Streaming Lens report — 'vi-2026' for Vertical Invasion 2026 (micro-drama / vertical drama), 'africa-2026' for Africa Streaming 2026 (African OTT). This stores the email, sends an email, and adds the visitor to the mailing list — ask the visitor and pass their explicit consent before calling it. Returns the signed download URL for the teaser PDF and fills the page's own email gate so the visitor sees what was submitted.

consent.description: Must be true, and must reflect consent the visitor actually gave for this email to be stored and used.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: Fetch the content, key findings, and metadata of a specific market analysis or guide article (params: slug, url) -> {title, url, summary, sections: [{heading, content}]}

url.description: Full URL of the article to fetch.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Retrieve pricing tiers for reports, MCP data silo subscriptions, advisory, and consulting (params: none) -> {currency, tiers: [{name, price, billing, description, cta_url}]}

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Get detailed information, table of contents/headings, and summary for a specific report (params: report_id) -> {id, title, url, teaser_url, key_sections, summary}

tools.name: list_reports
tools.description: List all strategic intelligence reports published or in progress (params: status) -> list [{id, title, status, pages, market_size, url}]

status.description: Filter by status, e.g. 'LIVE' or 'ENRICHING'

tools.name: start_call_booking
tools.description: Initiate scheduling a strategic consultation or advisory call with the author (params: navigate=true) -> {status: 'handoff', booking_url: string}

navigate.description: Whether to redirect the browser to the calendar booking interface.

tools.name: submit_datapoint_challenge
tools.description: Prepare a formal challenge or correction to a specific sourced datapoint on the site (params: datapoint_id, proposed_value, source_url, notes) -> {status: 'ready', datapoint_id: string, challenge_url: string}

notes.description: Context or explanation of the challenge.

source_url.description: Authoritative source link backing the correction.

proposed_value.description: Your corrected or proposed metric value.

sites.name: lobby.host
sites.description: Lobby greets every visitor, understands what they need, and hands you the lead. Built on WebMCP, so the AI agents they bring get the same answers.

tools.name: ask_concierge
tools.description: Ask this business's concierge a question in natural language — hours, policies, recommendations, anything a guest would ask at the desk. Replies come from the same knowledge and conversation engine the human-facing chat on this page uses, and context is kept across calls so follow-ups work. Use this for judgement and nuance. Do NOT use it for facts the free lookup tools already return — prefer get_business_info for contact details and list_offerings for services, which are instant and cost nothing. Returns { ok, answer, conversation_id }.

question.description: The visitor's question, in natural language. One question per call; the concierge answers conversationally.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this reply belongs to. Stable across calls on this page.

tools.name: get_business_info
tools.description: Verified public facts about this business: name, how it introduces itself, published contact details, the topics it invites questions about, and whether it can take a booking. Free and instant, no conversation started. Call this FIRST for anything factual — it is cheaper and more reliable than asking the concierge. Returns { ok, name, introduction, contact { email, phone, url }, suggested_topics[], booking_available }. Every Lobby tool returns that same envelope: `ok`, plus `error` with `code` and `message` when `ok` is false, alongside its own payload.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

introduction.description: How the business introduces itself to a visitor.

contact.description: Published contact details, or null if none.

suggested_topics.description: Topics this concierge is prepared to discuss.

booking_available.description: True when this concierge exposes booking tools. When false, nothing here can be scheduled — offer the contact details instead of implying a booking is possible.

tools.name: list_offerings
tools.description: The services this business offers, as structured data an agent can compare, filter or present. Each offering carries an explicit `bookable` flag — check it before attempting to schedule anything. Free and instant. Returns { ok, offerings[] of { id, name, description, price, currency, bookable, action_url, contact_required }, total, booking_available }.

bookable_only.description: When true, return only offerings that can be scheduled through the booking tools. Default false (return all).

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

offerings.description: The business’s services, comparable and filterable.

id.description: Stable id to pass to other tools.

price.description: Null when the business does not publish a price.

bookable.description: True only when this specific offering can be scheduled through the booking tools. Never assume a bookable offering from the presence of a booking tool.

contact_required.description: True when arranging this offering needs a human — use the contact details from get_business_info.

booking_available.description: Whether this concierge can book at all. False means every offering is contact-only regardless of its own flag.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Lobby's plans: prices, monthly conversation allowances, what each tier includes, and what happens on going over. Authoritative and free — use this rather than reading prices off the page, and rather than asking the concierge. Returns { ok, currency, plans[] of { id, name, price_monthly, price_annual, monthly_conversations, shows_lobby_badge, includes_booking, features[], signup_url }, overage, what_counts_as_a_conversation }.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

includes_booking.description: Whether concierges on this plan can take bookings.

tools.name: recommend_plan
tools.description: Which Lobby plan fits a described business, and why. Deterministic — it compares the stated needs against the published allowances and features, it does not guess. Prefer this over asking the concierge "which plan should I pick", which cannot see the numbers. Returns { ok, recommended_plan_id, recommended_plan_name, price_monthly, reasons[], caveats[], signup_url }.

expected_monthly_conversations.description: Roughly how many visitor sessions a month. One visitor session is one conversation however many messages it holds.

number_of_sites.description: How many websites need a concierge.

needs_own_branding.description: True when the business wants the "Built with Lobby" footer gone.

needs_booking.description: True when visitors should be able to book an appointment through the concierge.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

reasons.description: Why this plan, in order of weight.

caveats.description: Things the visitor should know before committing. May be empty.

tools.name: get_setup_instructions
tools.description: How a business puts Lobby on its website: the one-line embed script for an existing site, or the hosted concierge page for a business without one. Returns { ok, options[] of { id, name, when_to_use, steps[], snippet }, signup_url } — the actual steps and the snippet shape, not a summary of them.

has_existing_website.description: True narrows the answer to the embed route, false to the hosted page. Omit for both.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

tools.name: list_customer_examples
tools.description: Live Lobby concierges an agent or a person can actually visit and try. Real published pages, not testimonials. Use these as proof when a visitor asks "who is using this" or "show me one working". Returns { ok, examples[] of { slug, url, agent_tools_available }, total }.

limit.description: How many to return. Default 6.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

agent_tools_available.description: Every hosted concierge page registers WebMCP tools, so an agent can visit and use it directly.

tools.name: open_signup
tools.description: The URL to start a Lobby account, and optionally navigate there. Signup is free and needs only an email address — no card. This is not a committing action, but it does move the visitor off the current page when `navigate` is true, so prefer returning the URL and letting them click unless they asked to be taken there. Returns { ok, url, navigated, requirements[] }.

plan.description: Which plan to start on. Default free.

navigate.description: When true, navigate this page to signup. Default false — navigating away ends the current conversation.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

requirements.description: What the visitor needs in order to sign up.

tools.name: get_booking_options
tools.description: What can be booked with this business, and for how long. Returns the bookable appointment types with their durations. Call this before check_availability — availability is always relative to one booking type, because duration determines which slots fit. Returns { ok, booking_types[] of { id, name, description, duration_minutes, price, currency, location_kind }, timezone }.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

timezone.description: IANA zone the business keeps its hours in. Slot times are returned as absolute UTC instants regardless, so a visitor in another zone is never offered a time that does not exist.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Free times for one booking type in a date range. Every slot is a real opening: the business’s published hours minus anything already on its calendar. An empty list is a definite "nothing free in that range", not an error — widen the range or offer to take a message. Returns { ok, slots[] of { start_utc, end_utc, start_local }, total, timezone, searched { from_date, to_date } }.

to_date.description: Last date to consider, YYYY-MM-DD, INCLUSIVE. Omit for a single day. At most 60 days after from_date.

visitor_timezone.description: The visitor's IANA timezone, if known (e.g. 'Europe/Berlin'). Slot times are echoed in it for display. Omit and the business’s own zone is used.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

start_local.description: Same instant, formatted in visitor_timezone, for showing a person. Never pass this back — pass start_utc.

tools.name: start_booking
tools.description: Book one of the free slots from check_availability. THIS COMMITS the visitor to an appointment and emails the business, so it is deliberately two-step: call it first WITHOUT `confirmed`, show the returned summary to the visitor in their own words, and only call it again with `confirmed: true` once they have explicitly agreed. Never set `confirmed: true` on the first call, and never infer agreement from the visitor merely having asked about times. Returns { ok, status, summary { what, when_utc, duration_minutes, guest_name, guest_email, business }, booking_id }. The visitor is emailed a confirmation with a calendar invitation attached and their own cancellation link. `cancel_url` is null here and stays null on purpose: that link is the visitor’s only credential for their appointment and it is not handed to a tool caller. If the visitor later wants to cancel, ask them for the token in that email and use cancel_booking — do not send them to the business, and do not try their booking_id.

start_utc.description: Exactly as returned by check_availability. Do not construct or round this yourself.

guest_name.description: The name the visitor gave you, as they gave it. This is what the business will see on the appointment.

guest_email.description: Where the confirmation goes. Ask the visitor; never invent, guess or reuse an address from elsewhere on the page.

notes.description: Anything the business should know beforehand.

confirmed.description: The visitor has seen the summary and explicitly agreed. Omit or false on the first call.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

status.description: `needs_confirmation` means NOTHING was booked yet. `booked` means the appointment exists, is on the business’s calendar, and a confirmation email has gone to the address given — carrying a calendar invitation and the visitor’s own cancellation link. Tell them to expect it. The appointment itself does not depend on that email: `booked` is the record, and a mail delay is not a booking that failed.

summary.description: Exactly what will be, or has been, booked. Read this back to the visitor verbatim before confirming.

tools.name: cancel_booking
tools.description: Cancel an appointment the visitor already has, using the cancellation token from their own confirmation email. THIS RELEASES the slot, tells the business, and cannot be undone, so it is two-step exactly like start_booking: call it first WITHOUT `confirmed`, read the returned summary back to the visitor, and only call it again with `confirmed: true` once they have explicitly agreed. Ask the visitor for the cancellation link or token from their confirmation email — that token is the ONLY thing that authorises this, and a booking id will not work and must not be tried. Never guess, construct, or reuse a token, and never take one from anywhere but the visitor you are speaking to. Returns { ok, status, summary { business, cancels, when_utc } }.

cancel_token.description: The token from the visitor’s confirmation email — either the token itself or the last path segment before /cancel in their cancellation link. This is a secret belonging to that one appointment. It is NOT the booking_id that start_booking returns, and passing an id here is refused.

confirmed.description: The visitor has seen the summary and explicitly agreed to cancel. Omit or false on the first call.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

status.description: `needs_confirmation` means NOTHING was cancelled yet and the appointment still stands. `cancelled` means the slot is free again, the calendar entry is gone, and both the visitor and the business have been emailed. Cancelling twice is safe and reports `cancelled` both times — the backend is idempotent, so a repeated call is never an error and never a second cancellation.

summary.description: What will be, or has been, cancelled. Read this back to the visitor before confirming.

cancels.description: Plain-language description of the appointment the token belongs to, for reading aloud.

when_utc.description: When the cancelled appointment was to start, as the backend reports it. NULL before confirmation: nothing previews a booking by token, so the time is genuinely not known until the cancellation is made. Do not invent a time for the visitor on the first call — ask them to confirm from their own email instead.

audience.description: Optional developmental range or audience group.

format.description: Optional format such as Activity, Cards, Poster, or Guided worksheet.

query.description: The practice situation or transition to work through.

tools.description: Retrieve one publication-gated evidence record with its status, confidence, fact-check and review dates, Practice Hub page, and official-source citations. Supports general practice guidance and reviewed state research.

query.description: Optional claim, topic, publisher, or source to search.

identifier.description: Optional exact claim ID returned by this or another Practice Hub tool.

jurisdiction.description: Optional state, federal, national, or jurisdiction-independent scope.

state.description: Optional state name or two-letter code.

query.description: The task or worksheet content to find.

query.description: Optional workflow, feature, or practice need.

products.description: Optional product names or slugs to compare.

tools.name: get_practice_hub_updates

query.description: Optional topic or affected resource to filter updates.

sites.name: sundaytable.openai.chatgpt.site

tools.name: list_meal_slots

day.description: A full day name, Monday through Sunday.

tools.name: upsert_recipe

recipeId.description: Stable recipe ID. Generated when omitted.

tools.name: set_meal

day.description: A full day name, Monday through Sunday.

day.description: A full day name, Monday through Sunday.

mealType.description: The lunch or dinner meal slot.

day.description: A full day name, Monday through Sunday.

sites.name: waisa.ca
sites.description: Waísa makes clean, naturally caffeinated guayusa tea from the Amazon. Smooth flavour, steady energy, and simple ingredients.

tools.name: find_waisa_stockists
tools.description: Find Canadian retailers and cafés that stock Waísa guayusa. Every stockist carries the full ready-to-drink can lineup (Vibrant Peach, Golden Pineapple, Wildberry Mint). Search by city, province name or code (Ontario, ON), postal code with or without a space, store name, flavour, or rank nearby stores by latitude and longitude. Returns named stores, addresses, directions URLs, and the matching city page so a Canadian user can walk in.

location.description: A Canadian city, province (Ontario or ON), postal code (V6B 1A1 or V6B1A1), "City, ON", store name, or street.

product.description: Optional flavour name. Every stockist carries Vibrant Peach, Golden Pineapple, and Wildberry Mint.

latitude.description: Latitude used with longitude to rank stores by distance.

longitude.description: Longitude used with latitude to rank stores by distance.

limit.description: Maximum number of stockists to return. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: learn_about_guayusa_energy
tools.description: Return facts about guayusa: what it is, why its naturally caffeinated energy can feel different, key whole-leaf compounds, Kichwa tradition, and preparation methods. Read-only product education; does not navigate or change the page.

topic.description: The guayusa topic to return. Defaults to all.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to update_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to update_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.
The option selections that were resolved to a variant, if provided.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

id.description: Cart GID.
Cart line GID from get_cart. Pass back to update_cart as line_items[].id to update or remove this line.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

line_price.description: Total price for the line (quantity × unit_price).

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

line_items.description: Items to add or update (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

deduped.description: True when this exact add was applied moments ago and was skipped to avoid a duplicate. When true, nothing changed on this call and updated is false.

line_items.description: Items added by this mutation, with product/variant details filled in from the post-mutation cart.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

resolved_items.description: Present only on the clarification-needed path (nothing was applied). Items that could have been added, with pre-mutation lookup titles when available.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

tools.name: ExecuteCode
tools.description: Start JavaScript in the Runme AppKernel sandbox and return a JSON operation snapshot. Read notebooks with notebooks.get({ uri }) and access cells through doc.notebook.cells; notebooks.read is not an API. Call await notebooks.help() when uncertain. Fast work completes inline. Long work continues by default after timeoutMs and can be polled with GetExecuteCodeOperation. Every accepted request returns a Runme-assigned operationId.

code.description: AppKernel JavaScript. For notebook reads, use await notebooks.get({ uri }) and doc.notebook.cells. Do not call notebooks.read; it does not exist. Use await notebooks.help() to inspect the live API.

timeoutMs.description: Optional initial response wait budget in milliseconds. Defaults to 15000 and is capped at 60000. It is not the hard execution deadline.

timeoutBehavior.description: What to do when timeoutMs expires. continue returns a running operation for later polling; cancel aborts the sandbox. Defaults to continue.

maxRuntimeMs.description: Hard runtime limit for the operation in milliseconds. Defaults to 600000 and is capped at 3600000.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional caller token for safely deduplicating a retried request. Runme still assigns the operationId.

tools.name: GetExecuteCodeOperation
tools.description: Poll an ExecuteCode operation by its Runme-assigned operationId. Use afterSequence to retrieve only new stdout/stderr events and waitMs for bounded long polling.

afterSequence.description: Return output events after this sequence number. Defaults to 0.

waitMs.description: Wait up to this many milliseconds for new output or a state change. Defaults to 0.

maxBytes.description: Maximum retained output bytes to return in this poll. Minimum 16384; defaults to 65536.

tools.name: CancelExecuteCodeOperation
tools.description: Request cancellation of an ExecuteCode sandbox operation. Cancellation is idempotent and does not guarantee that a downstream notebook, deployment, or cloud operation also stopped.

afterSequence.description: Return output events after this sequence number. Defaults to 0.

maxBytes.description: Maximum retained output bytes to return with the cancellation result. Minimum 16384; defaults to 65536.

tools.name: getDocumentation
tools.description: Codex, Claude, and other AI agents should invoke this read-only function with a name returned by listDocumentation to get that Runme documentation page as Markdown.

name.description: File or folder name to search for.

itemType.description: Restrict matches to files, folders, or either.

exactName.description: Match the complete name instead of searching for a contained phrase.

parentFolderIdOrUri.description: Optional parent folder ID or URI used to scope the search.

pageToken.description: Opaque token returned by the previous page.

folderIdOrUri.description: Google Drive folder ID or folder URI.

pageToken.description: Opaque token returned by the previous page.

tools.name: mountDriveFolder
tools.description: Validate, mirror, and add a specific Google Drive folder to the Runme workspace explorer. Pass only a folder ID or folder URL selected from user input or an unambiguous search result. The operation is idempotent for an already-mounted folder.

folderIdOrUri.description: Google Drive folder ID or folder URI from the user or an unambiguous search result.

Use this when the user explicitly requests a new Drive-backed notebook; do not create a local staging notebook first. Reuse the idempotency key for same-profile retries, and do not issue the same create concurrently from unrelated browser profiles.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to update_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to update_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.
